  • Troubleshoot if your device doesn’t ring
  • Learn about call & meeting encryption in Google Meet

Host controls

Add co-hosts in Google Meet

Add co-hosts in Google Meet

Host Management is available to all Google Workspace Editions. When Host Management is turned on, meeting hosts can use the following safety features:

  • Chat lock
  • Present lock
  • Audio lock
  • Video lock
  • End meeting for everyone
  • Mute everyone Some Workspace editions can use Host Management to add up to 25 co-hosts to their Google Meet meetings.
Eligibility
The following Workspace editions can add co-hosts:

  • Business Standard

  • Business Plus

  • Essentials

  • Enterprise Starter

  • Enterprise Essentials

  • Enterprise Standard

  • Enterprise Plus

  • All Workspace for education editions

  • Workspace Individual Important:

  • Based on your Google Workspace edition, Host Management might be on or off by default. Host Management can be turned on or off from inside a meeting. Workspace Admins can set up defaults for their domain.

  • Participants must be in the meeting to become a host. Classroom meeting hosts can make teachers co-hosts before a meeting.

  • Co-hosts can turn Host Management off. Only the main host can re-enable Host Management for all other hosts.

  • Participants can’t be appointed or removed as co-hosts from Breakout Rooms. Participants must return to the main room to be granted hosting privileges.

  • Only the main host receives meeting info, like attendance reports or polling details, but can share meeting info with other co-hosts.

  • Host Management settings are saved for any recurring meetings or meetings that re-use the same meeting code. Appointed co-hosts will need to be re-appointed for any recurring meetings.

  • We recommend you turn on Host Management settings before you use Breakout rooms. Settings for Host Management can’t be changed after Breakout rooms are live. This prevents the designation of co-hosts who can run Breakout rooms or use meeting safety features.

  • For meetings with host management switched off, anyone inside your organization can record a meeting. To allow anyone outside your organization to record a meeting, you must promote them to a co-host. If host management is on, only the main host and promoted co-hosts can record a meeting.

Share Meeting Artifacts with co-hosts

Certain Google Meet features generate Meeting Artifacts, which:

  • Are automatically shared with the primary meeting host.

  • Include Meet recordings, attendance reports, polling reports, and other documents etc. If you want co-hosts to get Meeting Artifacts, you must:

  • Have Host Management turned on before somebody can be added as a co-host.

  • Add them as co-hosts when you set up or edit the event in Google Calendar.

  • Select the artifact sharing checkbox when you add co-hosts in Google Calendar. Important:

  • If you promote someone to a co-host during an ongoing meeting, they won’t get Meeting Artifacts for that particular meeting. You must add them as a co-host when you set up or edit the event in Google Calendar.

  • If a participant’s co-host status is removed during the meeting, they still get Meeting Artifacts. They won’t receive artifacts for any future meetings that use the same code.

  • Co-hosts added to a series of ongoing meetings get Meeting Artifacts for future meetings that use the same code.

  • For Google Classroom meetings, all co-teachers are recognized as co-hosts and automatically get Meeting Artifacts. Their co-host status can’t be removed within Google Classroom.

    • If a user is removed as a co-teacher, they no longer receive meeting artifacts.

  • This setting is ignored while using Take Notes with Gemini.

To add co-hosts and share Meeting Artifacts:

Important: You can only do this on a computer.

  • On your desktop browser, go to Google Calendar.
  • Click the event or meeting you want to add a co-host to.
  • From the pop-up menu, click Edit event .
    • If your event doesn’t have a meeting attached, click Add Google Meet video conferencing.
  • Click Video call options .
  • In the pop-up menu, turn on Host Management .
  • On the left, click Co-hosts .
  • Check the box next to “Call artifacts are shared with the host and co-hosts you add here.”
  • Add participants as co-hosts.
Add a co-host before a meeting starts

Important: We highly recommend that you add a co-host before the meeting starts.

Add a co-host to a new meeting
  • On your desktop browser, go to Google Calendar.
  • At the top left, click Create.
  • In the drop down, select Event.
  • Add meeting guests.
    • If your event doesn’t have a meeting attached, click Add Google Meet video conferencing.
  • Click Video call options .
  • In the pop-up menu, turn on Host Management .
  • On the left, click Co-hosts .
  • Enter the names of the participants you want to add as a co-host.
  • Select their names from the drop down.
  • Click Save from within the pop-up menu.
  • To save the Google Calendar event, click Save
Add a co-host to an existing meeting

Important: You’ll have to be the creator of the meeting to make this change. If somebody else created the meeting then either they can add you as a co-host or transfer the meeting to you before you add co-hosts.

  • On your desktop browser, go to Google Calendar.
  • Click the event or meeting you want to add a co-host to.
  • From the pop-up menu, click Edit event .
    • If your event doesn’t have a meeting attached, click Add Google Meet video conferencing.
  • Click Video call options .
  • In the pop-up menu, turn on Host Management .
  • On the left, click on Co-hosts .
  • Enter the names of the participants you want to add as a co-host.
  • Select their name from the drop down.
  • Click Save from within the pop-up menu.
  • To save the Google Calendar event, click Save.
Use Host Management in a meeting
Turn Host Management on or off
  • On your computer, go to meet.google.com.
  • Join a meeting.
  • At the bottom right, click Host controls .
  • From the side panel that appears, switch on Host management .
  • To switch off, click Host Management Turn it off .
Add or remove a co-host
  • In a meeting, at the bottom right, click Show everyone .
  • From the “People” tab, find or search the participant’s name.
  • Next to their name, click Menu Grant host controls . Once the new co-hosts are granted hosting privileges, the Host controls icon appears at the bottom of their screen.

Add or remove people from a Google Meet meeting or call

Add or remove people from a Google Meet meeting or call

You can add people to a video meeting in Google Meet before or after the meeting starts. You can also remove people during a video meeting.

Some people need to request permission before they can join the video meeting. For details, go to Join a video meeting.

Add people to a video meeting in progress

Add people to a meeting

  • From the top right corner of your meeting screen, click People Add people.

  • Enter the name or email address Send email. Share joining info

  • At the bottom right, click meeting details .

  • Click Copy joining info.

  • Paste the meeting details into an email, or other app, and send. Add a phone participant to a meeting in progress

You can add someone by phone to a Google Meet video meeting in certain countries and regions.

  • After you join the meeting, at the bottom right, click People .
  • Click Add people Call .
  • In the window, select the country you’re calling to add the country code and enter the phone number for the person that you want to call.
  • Click Call .
Supported countries and regions

For a complete list of countries and regions, go to Supported countries for adding guests by phone.

Bulk admit participants to a Google Meet meeting

You can bulk admit participants and students into a Google Meet meeting. Only the meeting organizer can find or approve requests to join a meeting. The meeting organizer should stay in the meeting to approve requests.

  • When a request to join the meeting appears, click Admit or Deny entry.
  • Click View all when you have multiple participants waiting to join the meeting. Choose an option:
    • Next to the name, click Admit or Deny entry to admit or deny participants one at a time.
    • Click Admit all or Deny all to admit or deny all participants at the same time.
Remove people during a video meeting

Important: For meetings with Host Management on, only a meeting host or co-host can remove another participant from an ongoing meeting. If Host Management is off, anyone from the meeting organizers’ domain can remove a participant.

Remove meeting participants or presentations
  • Hover over a person’s or presentation’s tile.
  • Click More options Remove from the call.
Remove participants or presentations not on the layout
  • At the bottom right, click Show everyone .
  • Next to the participant you want to remove, click More actions .
  • Select Remove from the call.
  • On the box that opens, select one or more of the following options:
    • To just remove a participant, select Remove.
    • To remove and mark a participant as abusive, select Fill out an abuse report.
    • To make sure a participant doesn’t rejoin the same meeting, select Block.
      • Important: If you block a user, they are only blocked from the current meeting or concurrent meetings which use the same meeting code. They can still join other meetings you host. To allow users to rejoin a meeting they are blocked from, they must be manually re-invited from within the meeting. Google Workspace for Education users: If a participant’s requests to join a meeting are denied twice, they won’t be able to request to join the meeting again. In these cases, the meeting organizer can manually invite them back into the meeting.
End meeting for all

Important: Host Management must be turned on to use End meeting for all.

Hosts can end the meeting for everyone on a Google Meet meeting. ‘End the call for everyone’ ends the meeting and automatically removes all participants, so that the hosts don’t have to remove participants manually.

Best practices

  • Participants can access the meeting link for a meeting that has ended, but can’t join until the meeting host restarts the meeting. The meeting will automatically restart once the host re-joins.
  • To make sure students can’t access the end-meeting feature to start or end meetings, admins can turn off the “Create a meeting” setting for students.
  • Some Workspace admins on certain Workspace editions can end a meeting with the Security Investigation Tool. Learn how to use the investigation tool.
  • Create a new meeting each time you want to meet with a different group of participants. When you restart an ended meeting, all previous participants can join.
To end a meeting for all:
  • On the bottom, click Leave call .
  • On the window that appears, click End meeting for all.
  • To leave the meeting but not end it for everyone, click Leave meeting. Tip: End meeting for all will also end any open breakout rooms. If there are a lot of Breakout rooms open, the main room will end first and all other Breakout rooms may take up to a few minutes to end.

Computer AndroidiPhone & iPad

Add or remove people from a Google Meet meeting or call (Android)

Add or remove people from a Google Meet meeting or call

You can add people to a video meeting in Google Meet before or after the meeting starts. You can also remove people during a video meeting.

Some people need to request permission before they can join the video meeting. For details, go to Join a video meeting.

Add people during a video meeting

While in the meeting, you can invite others to join. For meetings organized through personal Google accounts, only the meeting organizer can admit participants. For meetings organized through a Google Workspace account, only someone from within the organization can admit a participant who isn’t in the same organization.

  • Open the Meet app and join a meeting.
  • On the top left, tap the meeting name.
  • On the “People” tab, to send the meeting details to other participants, tap Share invite . Tip: For meetings organized by Google Workspace users, the joining info includes how to join via a phone.
Share the invite if no one has joined yet
  • On your Android phone or tablet, open the Meet app .
  • Join a meeting.
  • If no one else is in the meeting, the message “You’re the only one here” shows.
  • To send the meeting details to other participants, tap Share invite .
Ring someone to join into an ongoing meeting or call

  • On your Android phone or tablet, open the Meet app .

  • Join a meeting or call.

  • To find the controls, tap the screen.

  • At the top left, tap the Header Add people .

  • Select a contact or enter a phone number.

  • Tap Call. The “Add people” icon is not available in certain situations:

  • If “Host management” is turned on in a meeting and you aren’t the host.

  • If client-side encryption or additional encryption is in use.

  • If you join as a guest and aren’t logged in.

  • If you can’t call because of meeting restrictions.

Remove people during a video meeting

Important: For meetings with Host Management on, only a meeting host or co-host can remove another participant from an ongoing meeting. If Host Management is off, anyone from the meeting organizers’ domain can remove a participant.

  • At the top left, tap the meeting name or meeting code.
  • Next to the participant you want to remove, tap Actions .
  • Tap Remove .
  • On the box that opens, select one or more of the following options:
  • To just remove a participant, select Remove.
  • To remove and mark a participant as abusive, select Fill out an abuse report.
  • To make sure a participant doesn’t rejoin the same meeting, select Block.
    • Important: If you block a user, they are only blocked from the current meeting or concurrent meetings which use the same meeting code. They can still join other meetings you host. To allow users to rejoin a meeting they are blocked from, they must be manually re-invited from within the meeting. Google Workspace for Education users: If a participant’s requests to join a meeting are denied twice, they won’t be able to request to join the meeting again. In these cases, the meeting organizer can manually invite them back into the meeting.
End meeting for all

Important: To end meeting for all you must:

  • Turn on “Host management.”
  • Be a meeting organizer or moderator on an Android device. To end the meeting and automatically remove all participants, click End meeting for all.

Learn about best practices

  • Participants can access the meeting link for a meeting that has ended, but can’t join until the meeting host restarts the meeting. The meeting automatically restarts once the host rejoins.

  • To make sure that students can’t access the end-meeting feature to start or end meetings, admins can turn off the “Create a meeting” setting for students.

  • Some Workspace admins on certain Workspace editions can end a meeting with the security investigation tool. Learn how to use the investigation tool.

  • Create a new meeting each time you want to meet with a different group of participants. When you restart a meeting, all previous participants can join. To end a meeting for all:

  • In a Google Meet, at the bottom of your screen, tap Leave call .

  • On the menu that appears, tap End the call. Optional: To leave the meeting but not end it for everyone, tap Just leave the call.

Add or remove people from a Google Meet meeting or call (Computer)

Add or remove people from a Google Meet meeting or call

You can add people to a video meeting in Google Meet before or after the meeting starts. You can also remove people during a video meeting.

Some people need to request permission before they can join the video meeting. For details, go to Join a video meeting.

Add people to a video meeting in progress

Add people to a meeting

  • From the top right corner of your meeting screen, click People Add people.

  • Enter the name or email address Send email. Share joining info

  • At the bottom right, click meeting details .

  • Click Copy joining info.

  • Paste the meeting details into an email, or other app, and send. Add a phone participant to a meeting in progress

You can add someone by phone to a Google Meet video meeting in certain countries and regions.

  • After you join the meeting, at the bottom right, click People .
  • Click Add people Call .
  • In the window, select the country you’re calling to add the country code and enter the phone number for the person that you want to call.
  • Click Call .
Supported countries and regions

For a complete list of countries and regions, go to Supported countries for adding guests by phone.

Bulk admit participants to a Google Meet meeting

You can bulk admit participants and students into a Google Meet meeting. Only the meeting organizer can find or approve requests to join a meeting. The meeting organizer should stay in the meeting to approve requests.

  • When a request to join the meeting appears, click Admit or Deny entry.
  • Click View all when you have multiple participants waiting to join the meeting. Choose an option:
    • Next to the name, click Admit or Deny entry to admit or deny participants one at a time.
    • Click Admit all or Deny all to admit or deny all participants at the same time.
Remove people during a video meeting

Important: For meetings with Host Management on, only a meeting host or co-host can remove another participant from an ongoing meeting. If Host Management is off, anyone from the meeting organizers’ domain can remove a participant.

Remove meeting participants or presentations
  • Hover over a person’s or presentation’s tile.
  • Click More options Remove from the call.
Remove participants or presentations not on the layout
  • At the bottom right, click Show everyone .
  • Next to the participant you want to remove, click More actions .
  • Select Remove from the call.
  • On the box that opens, select one or more of the following options:
    • To just remove a participant, select Remove.
    • To remove and mark a participant as abusive, select Fill out an abuse report.
    • To make sure a participant doesn’t rejoin the same meeting, select Block.
      • Important: If you block a user, they are only blocked from the current meeting or concurrent meetings which use the same meeting code. They can still join other meetings you host. To allow users to rejoin a meeting they are blocked from, they must be manually re-invited from within the meeting. Google Workspace for Education users: If a participant’s requests to join a meeting are denied twice, they won’t be able to request to join the meeting again. In these cases, the meeting organizer can manually invite them back into the meeting.
End meeting for all

Important: Host Management must be turned on to use End meeting for all.

Hosts can end the meeting for everyone on a Google Meet meeting. ‘End the call for everyone’ ends the meeting and automatically removes all participants, so that the hosts don’t have to remove participants manually.

Best practices

  • Participants can access the meeting link for a meeting that has ended, but can’t join until the meeting host restarts the meeting. The meeting will automatically restart once the host re-joins.
  • To make sure students can’t access the end-meeting feature to start or end meetings, admins can turn off the “Create a meeting” setting for students.
  • Some Workspace admins on certain Workspace editions can end a meeting with the Security Investigation Tool. Learn how to use the investigation tool.
  • Create a new meeting each time you want to meet with a different group of participants. When you restart an ended meeting, all previous participants can join.
To end a meeting for all:
  • On the bottom, click Leave call .
  • On the window that appears, click End meeting for all.
  • To leave the meeting but not end it for everyone, click Leave meeting. Tip: End meeting for all will also end any open breakout rooms. If there are a lot of Breakout rooms open, the main room will end first and all other Breakout rooms may take up to a few minutes to end.

Apply watermarks to your meetings

Apply watermarks to your meetings

Important: This feature requires an eligible Google Workspace subscription through your work or school. If you can’t find this feature, contact your administrator.

A watermark is a subtle text overlay that’s applied to your video feed and presentations when you’re in a meeting. It displays the meeting’s meet code and the email address of the viewer. You can use a watermark to:

  • Protect the confidentiality of the visual content you share in a meeting.
  • Help trace unauthorized copies of video and screen shares. Please note that this doesn’t prevent the removal of the watermark by a user who has a program to edit images.

To enable watermarks, make sure that participants:

  • Are signed in to a Google Account
  • Use either the latest version of the mobile app or an updated Chromium browser Otherwise, you get a prompt to remove them from the meeting once you enable the watermark. If a participant uses an unsupported browser, they can’t view incoming video and presentations.

You can’t use watermarks if you:

  • Record a meeting.
  • Live stream a meeting. If you start to record or live stream during a meeting, it disables the watermark.
Learn what you need to apply watermarks

Important:

  • Mobile users can only view watermarks. To enable this feature, use a computer.
  • Watermarks aren’t supported in Firefox. When watermarks are enabled on unsupported browsers, the participant can no longer view incoming video or presentations.
Add a watermark
  • In a meeting, at the bottom right, click Host controls .
    • If you join from a conference room, you can only enable watermarks through Companion mode. Learn more about Companion mode in Google Meet.
  • Turn on Add a watermark.
    • If a participant doesn’t meet the technical requirements, you’re prompted that “People will be removed from this call.”
      • You can select Cancel or Add the watermark anyway.

Ask participants questions in Google Meet

Ask participants questions in Google Meet

Want advanced Google Workspace features for your business?

Try Google Workspace today!

Important:

  • When you create a Q&A in a live stream, it’s automatically available to both meeting participants and live stream participants. Hosts can disable Q&A for live stream participants from their computer.
  • You can have a maximum of 500 questions per Q&A. Requirements to use Q&A in Google Meet

Important: Q&A in Google Meet is available for users with these Google Workspace editions:

  • Essentials
  • Business Standard
  • Business Plus
  • Enterprise Starter
  • Enterprise Essentials
  • Enterprise Standard
  • Enterprise Plus
  • Education Plus
  • Teaching and Learning Upgrade
  • G Suite Business
  • Nonprofits
  • Workspace Individual Tip: Workspace Admins can switch this feature on or off for their entire organization.
Ask participants questions in a Google Meet meeting

Anyone in a meeting can ask questions. The questions show until they’re deleted or hidden.

After a meeting, the moderator gets a detailed report of all the questions.

Anyone who schedules or starts a meeting will be the meeting host. If you transfer or schedule a meeting on someone else’s calendar, the other person could become the meeting host. By default, there’s only one meeting host per meeting but inside the meeting, you can add up to 25 co-hosts.

Turn on Q&A

Important:

  • Q&A turns on automatically for all users except Google Workspace for Education users. For Education users, Meeting hosts can turn on Q&A during the meeting.
  • Hosts can disable Q&A from a pop-up when they start the live stream from their computer or turn it off under “Host controls.”
  • On your computer, at the bottom right, click Host Controls .
  • Scroll to Meeting Activities.
  • Turn on Allow questions in Q&A . Tip: By default, questions can be asked anonymously. To stop this, turn off Allow anonymous questions (Q&A) .

Turn on Q&A on mobile

  • Tap More controls Host Controls .
  • Scroll to Meeting Activities.
  • Turn on Allow questions in Q&A . Tip: By default, questions can be asked anonymously. To stop this, turn off Allow anonymous questions (Q&A)
View & manage questions

Important: All asked questions are included in the Questions report emailed to the moderators after the meeting.

  • On your computer, at the bottom right, click Meeting tools Q&A.
  • To filter questions, next to “All questions,” click Down arrow .
  • Select an option:
    • To delete a question: On any question, click Delete .
      • Tip: You can only view deleted and anonymous deleted questions in the report, not in the actual meeting.
    • To upvote a question: On the question, click Upvote .
    • To hide a question: On the question, click Hide .
    • To mark a question answered: On the question, click Mark as answered .
      • Tip: Mark a question answered so participants know it was answered.
    • To sort questions by order or most upvotes:
      • Next to “Popular,” click Down arrow .
      • Select an option. View and manage questions on mobile

Important: All asked questions are included in the Questions report emailed to the moderators after the meeting.

  • Tap More controls Meeting tools Q&A.
  • To filter questions, next to “All questions,” tap Down arrow .
    • To delete a question: On any question, tap Delete .
      • Tip: You can only view deleted and anonymous deleted questions in the report, not in the actual meeting.
    • To upvote a question: On the question, tap Upvote .
    • To hide a question: On the question, tap Hide .
    • To mark a question answered: On the question, tap Mark as answered .
      • Tip: Mark a question answered so participants know it was answered.
    • To sort questions by order or most upvotes:
      • Next to “Popular”, tap Down arrow .
      • Select an option.
Moderate Q&A questions

During meetings and in livestreams, to review the questions before they’re shown to the meeting attendees moderate Q&A:

Important:

  • Moderation is off by default.

  • Hosts can only moderate through the web with a computer. To turn on moderation as a host after you’ve joined a meeting:

  • On your computer, at the bottom right, click Host Controls.

  • Scroll down to Meeting Activities.

  • To turn on question moderation, turn on Hide each question until a host approves . To moderate questions:

  • On your computer, find a question marked “Pending approval.”

  • Choose to Approve or Delete the question.

  • Tip: A host can’t bulk approve questions. Tip: A host can turn off question moderation from Host Controls during the meeting. Questions already asked won’t be affected by the change.

Ask a question

When you ask a question, everyone in the meeting gets a notification.

When you ask a question anonymously, details are hidden from:

  • Other meeting participants

  • The moderators

  • Your Workspace admin The question is shared in its entirety with Google. The question is later anonymized or deleted, subject to our data retention policy.

  • On your computer, at the bottom right, click Meeting tools Q&A Ask a question.

  • Enter your question click Post. Tip: To ask your question anonymously, check the option “Post Anonymously.”

Ask a question on mobile

  • Tap More controls Meeting tools Q&A Ask a question.
  • Enter your question tap Post. Tip: To ask your question anonymously, check the option “Post Anonymously.”
View a questions report

After the meeting, a question report is emailed to the moderator. The email includes a list of questions that were asked, hidden, moderator approved, or deleted along with the names of the people who posted the questions.

  • Open the email with the questions report.
  • Click the report attachment.

Assign moderated contributor roles in Google Meet

Assign moderated contributor roles in Google Meet

For the best experience, and to scale attendance for large meetings, enable all participants as moderated contributors. When you enable moderated contributor roles, you get the option to also designate some attendees as contributors.

Moderated contributors can:

  • Observe the meeting
  • Raise their hand
  • Participate in activities, such as Q&A and polls
  • Use reactions Tip: When you are in a moderated contributor role, at the bottom, next to the meeting name, “View only” displays.

Participants can’t:

  • Share audio or video
  • Share their screen
  • Chat Learn which Google Workspace editions have the moderated contributor role

You can pre-set meeting attendees as viewers in the following Workspace editions:

  • Google Workspace Business Standard
  • Business Plus
  • Enterprise Standard
  • Enterprise Essentials
  • Education Fundamentals
  • Education Standard
  • Teaching & Learning upgrade
  • Education Plus
  • Enterprise Essentials Plus
  • Enterprise Plus Tip: In Enterprise Plus, Enterprise Essentials Plus, and Education Plus, after 500 contributors join, the next 500 automatically join in Viewer Mode.
Turn on Everyone is a moderated contributor
  • On your computer, open Google Calendar.
  • Create a new meeting and add guests.
  • In the Google Calendar meeting invite, open Host controls .
  • Turn on Host management.
  • In the “Guests” tab, turn on Everyone is a moderated contributor by default.
  • Optional: Add contributors.
    • To add contributors, add guests to the invite.
    • Tip: If their email doesn’t display, make sure they’re first added to the invite.
Change a participant from moderated contributor to contributor

Important: A host can move a moderated contributor into a contributor and back to a moderated contributor while on Web or when using Picture-in-Picture mode on the computer.

When a moderated contributor raises their hand, the host or co-host can make the moderated contributor a contributor.

As a host or co-host:

  • From the top right corner of your meeting screen, click People.
    • Important: Make sure to click on people. If you just hover over the people panel, you won’t be able to see the list of meeting attendees.
  • Select the participant Make a contributor .

Conduct polls in Google Meet

Conduct polls in Google Meet

Want advanced Google Workspace features for your business?

Try Google Workspace today!

Important:

  • When you create a poll in a live stream, it’s automatically available to both meeting participants and live stream participants. Hosts can’t disable polls for live stream users.
  • You can’t create, but can respond to polls on mobile devices. Requirements to use polls in Google Meet.

Important: Polling in Google Meet is available to these Google Workspace editions:

  • Essentials
  • Business Standard
  • Business Plus
  • Enterprise Starter
  • Enterprise Essentials
  • Enterprise Standard
  • Enterprise Plus
  • Education Plus
  • Teaching and Learning Upgrade
  • G Suite Business
  • Nonprofits
  • Workspace Individual Subscriber Tip: Workspace Admins can switch this feature on or off for their entire organization.
Conduct a poll in a Google Meet meeting

Polling in Google Meet using Google Workspace for business

For meeting moderators:

As a meeting moderator, you can create polls for participants to vote on. After the meeting, the moderator is automatically emailed a report of the poll results. The report contains names and answers of the participants. Participant names aren’t shared in the case of anonymous polls.

Anyone who schedules or starts a meeting will be the meeting host. If you transfer or schedule a meeting on someone else’s calendar, the other person could become the meeting host. By default, there is only one meeting host per meeting but you can add up to 25 co-hosts once inside the meeting.

Create a poll
  • In a meeting, at the bottom right, click Meeting tools click Polls.
  • Click Start a poll.
  • Enter a question and add options for the poll.
    • Tip: You can let users respond anonymously to Polls. Before you save or launch your poll, turn on Responses appear without names .
  • Choose one:
    • To post your poll, click Launch.
    • To save your poll so you can launch it later, click Save.
  • Tip: Polls you save remain listed under Polls for the duration of the meeting. After the call ends, all polls are permanently deleted. Meeting moderators are emailed a polling report at the end of the meeting.
  • After a poll is launched, to vote on your own poll, select one of the optionsclick Vote.
Moderate a poll
  • In a meeting, at the bottom right, click Meeting tools click Polls.
  • Optional: To let participants find a poll’s results, next to “Show everyone the results,” click Switch on .
  • Optional: To close a poll and not allow responses, click End the poll.
    • Tip: Participants can still find the poll.
  • To permanently delete a poll from your list of polls, click Delete .
    • Tip: No one can find deleted polls.
Get a poll report

After a meeting, the moderator is emailed a report for any polls conducted in the meeting. The report includes the names and answers of the meeting participants.

  • Open the poll report email.
  • Click the report attachment.
For meeting participants:

As a meeting participant, you can submit a response for a poll.

You’ll get a notification in the meeting when the moderator starts a poll. Be sure to submit your response before the poll or meeting ends.

Important: When you respond to a poll anonymously, details are hidden from:

  • Other meeting participants

  • The moderators

  • Your Workspace Admin Your response to a poll is shared in its entirety with Google. The poll is later anonymized or deleted, subject to our data retention policy.

  • In a meeting, at the bottom right, click Meeting tools click Polls.

  • In the poll, select your response click Vote.

  • Tip: After you click Vote, you can’t change your response. Computer AndroidiPhone & iPad

Lock audio & video in a Google Meet meeting

Lock audio & video in a Google Meet meeting

Important: To use Audio and Video Lock, you must first turn on Host Management.

As a meeting host or co-host, you can lock all participants’ audio and cameras so they’re muted and no one can turn on their video. Once you turn off Audio Lock, everyone can unmute their devices. Similarly, when you turn off Video Lock, everyone can use their camera again. Audio and Video Lock don’t apply to the meeting host or co-hosts. You can only set Audio and Video Lock from your computer or iOS device, but lock settings apply to all devices.

Lock participants’ audio & video

Important: When you turn on Audio or Video Lock, mobile participants may be removed from the meeting if their device doesn’t have:

  • The most updated version of the Meet or Gmail app
  • Android OS version M or newer
  • iOS version 12 or newer Once you turn Audio or Video Lock off, removed participants can rejoin.
Lock participants’ audio
  • During the meeting, from the bottom right, click Host Controls .
  • From the side panel that opens, toggle Turn on their microphone on or off. Tip: After you turn off Audio Lock, participants must manually turn on their microphones.
Lock participants’ video
  • During the meeting, from the bottom right, click Host Controls .
  • From the side panel that opens, toggle Turn on their video on or off. Tip: After you turn off Video Lock, participants must manually turn on their cameras.

Manage host controls

Manage host controls

All Google Workspace editions have Host management. When it’s turned on, meeting hosts can use settings to keep control of their meeting. Only hosts can access these controls:

  • Add or remove people
  • Manage chat moderation in a video meeting
  • Lock audio
  • Assign View only roles
  • Lock video
  • Add co-hosts
  • Ask participants questions Set up host controls before your Google Meet meeting
Turn Host management on or off

On Google Meet:

  • On your computer, go to Google Meet.

  • Join a meeting.

  • At the bottom right, click Host controls .

  • In the side panel, turn Host management on or off. On Google Calendar:

  • On your computer, go to Google Calendar.

  • To create a new Calendar event, at the top left, click Create Event Add Google Meet video conferencing .

  • Click Video call options .

  • On the left, select Host controls .

  • In the side panel, turn Host management on or off.

    • It’s off by default.

  • Click Save. Computer AndroidiPhone & iPad

Use add-ons with Google Meet

Use add-ons with Google Meet

On your computer or mobile device, you can use Google Meet add-ons to enhance collaboration, productivity, and the overall experience of your meetings.

Tip: For Meet users who have a Workspace admin, your admin may pre-install or restrict the usage of certain add-ons for you. Learn how admins can control your add-ons experience.

All users will find pre-installed 1P apps from Google by default on their device.

Eligibility

You can’t use add-ons if:

  • Your Workspace admin has blocked the add-on.
  • You use Meet through a Family Link account.
  • Your meeting host has assigned you a View only role.
  • You’re not signed in with a Google Account.
  • You’re under the age of consent in your country or region.
  • You are in a client-side encrypted meeting or attending a Live Stream event.
About third-party add-ons

Important: The Google Workspace Marketplace includes third-party add-ons that are compatible with Meet but not made by Google.

Add-ons that require third-party authentication may not work as expected. If you use Meet add-ons in Google Chrome Browser and it isn’t working:

  • Change your cookie settings to temporarily allow third-party cookies.

  • Reload and rejoin your meeting.

  • Re-open the add-on. For more help with a third-party add-on in the Google Workspace Marketplace:

  • Go to the add-ons page.

  • Scroll to the “Additional information” section.

  • Under “Support,” click the link.

Limitations & known issues

Use full screen

When you use an add-on, full screen mode won’t work when you:

  • Double click the screen to go full screen.

  • Click More controls Full Screen . To use full-screen mode:

  • At the top right corner of your Chrome browser, click Customize and control Google Chrome.

  • From the drop-down menu, click Full Screen . Use add-ons with Google Workspace for Education

At this time, you can’t enable third-party apps for users under 18 on Google Meet.

Use add-ons on different platforms

All add-ons don’t work across every platform.

  • When you’re on an unsupported platform, you’ll get this pop-notification: “Can’t join the activity.”
  • If you have an add-on installed on mobile that doesn’t currently work on a desktop device, it’ll be grayed out in the Tools panel and listed as an unavailable add-on.
Install a featured third-party add-on within Google Meet

Important: At the top of the “Tools” panel, you can find featured add-ons. When you install an add-on from the “Featured add-ons“ panel, the add-on will move to the “Installed add-ons” section.

  • At the bottom right, click Tools .
  • At the top of the “Tools” panel, click the featured add-on you want to install.
  • On the add-on page that opens within Meet, click Install.
    • You’ll notice a pop-up that asks you to select the Google Account you want to access the add-on in. Make sure that you select the same Google Account you used to join the meeting.
  • When prompted to “Allow the app to access your Google Account,” click Allow.
Install other third-party add-ons within Google Meet
  • At the bottom right, click Tools .
  • On the “Tools” panel, at the bottom, click .
  • On the “Google Workspace Marketplace” panel, click Search apps .
    • Tip: At the top right of the “Google Workspace Marketplace” panel, you’ll find the search bar.
  • Enter and search your add-on.
  • On the search results, click the add-on you want to install.
  • When the add-on page opens, click Install.
    • You’ll notice a pop-up that asks you to select the Google Account you want to use the add-on in. Make sure you select the same Google Account you used to join the meeting.
  • When prompted to “Allow the app to access your Google Account,” click Allow.
For Meeting Hosts
Start an activity with a third-party add-on
  • While in a meeting, at the bottom right, click Tools .
  • Click the add-on you want to use.
  • Based on the add-on you select, follow the conditional steps:
    • Depending on the third-party add-on you select, you’ll either be asked to sign in to the add-on app through your Google Account or you’ll be able to proceed without signing in. If the add-on app requires you to sign in, then follow the on-screen prompts to sign in to the third-party app.
    • Depending on the add-on, you’ll notice a new screen within the add-ons panel which will require you to select or input a few options.
      • Example: At this step, you can select a specific file to collaborate on with others.
    • Depending on the add-on, you may be required to share file access with other meeting guests. To give access, follow on-screen prompts.
  • After you complete the conditional steps, click your activity will begin.
  • When the pop-up message “Others who have the add-on installed can interact with the content on their main screen” appears, click Continue.
    • Other meeting participants can now collaborate with you while using the third-party add-on in Meet.
  • Optional but recommended: To make sure that participants who don’t have the add-on can observe the activity:
    • When an activity starts, on the banner, at the top of the ongoing add-on activity, click Screen share Allow.
  • To end the activity, on the banner, at the top of the ongoing add-on activity, click End activity. Tip: You can only collaborate on one add-on at a time.
Let meeting participants start add-on activities

All meeting participants can start add-on activities by default. Meeting hosts can choose to disallow other participants from starting an add-on activity. Presently, meeting hosts can only change this setting when using Meet on a desktop device:

  • On your computer, go to meet.google.com.
  • Join a meeting.
  • At the bottom right, click Host controls .
  • On the side panel that appears, toggle off “Let contributors share add-on activities” .
For Meeting Guests
Join an activity on a third-party add-on

If you have the add-on installed:

  • When the meeting host starts an activity, at the top right, click Join.

  • Start to collaborate on the file directly. If you don’t have the add-on installed:

  • When a meeting host starts an activity, at the top right corner, click Install and join.

  • From the pop up, click Install.

  • You’ll notice a pop-up that asks you to select the Google Account you want to use the add-on in.

    • Make sure you select the same Google Account you used to join the meeting.

  • When the add-on is installed, at the top right, click Join activity.

    • Based on the add-on you select:
      • You’ll be asked to sign in to the add-on app through your Google Account. Follow the on-screen prompts to sign in.
      • You can proceed without signing in. Tips: You can’t use a third-party add-on if:

  • Your Workspace Admin blocks you from using a particular add-on.

  • You use Meet with a Family Link account. If you use a Family Link account, you can’t install add-ons.

Leave an activity

Important: When you leave an activity, you’ll be sent back to the meeting. Hosts can also end an activity for all participants.

  • At the bottom right, click Tools .
  • Click Active add-on Leave activity.
Start an activity with a third-party add-on

All meeting participants can start add-on activities by default. Meeting hosts can choose to disallow other participants from starting an add-on activity. If you click an add-on and see an on-screen notification that says “You can’t use this add-on with others. Only a host can share add-on activities in this meeting.” it means that the host has currently disallowed you to use this feature.

  • While in a meeting, at the bottom right, click Tools .
  • Click the add-on you want to use.
  • Based on the add-on you select, follow the conditional steps:
    • Depending on the third-party add-on you select, you’ll either be asked to sign in to the add-on app through your Google Account or you’ll be able to proceed without signing in. If the add-on app requires you to sign in, then follow the on-screen prompts to sign in to the third-party app.
    • Depending on the add-on, you’ll notice a new screen within the add-ons panel which will require you to select or input a few options.
      • Example: At this step, you can select a specific file to collaborate on with others.
    • Depending on the add-on, you may be required to share file access with other meeting guests. To give access, follow on-screen prompts.
  • After you complete the conditional steps, click your activity will begin.
  • When the pop-up message “Others who have the add-on installed can interact with the content on their main screen” appears, click Continue.
    • Other meeting participants can now collaborate with you while using the third-party add-on in Meet.
  • Optional but recommended: To make sure that participants who don’t have the add-on can observe the activity:
    • When an activity starts, on the banner, at the top of the ongoing add-on activity, click Screen share Allow.
  • To end the activity, on the banner, at the top of the ongoing add-on activity, click End activity. Tip: You can only collaborate on one add-on at a time.

Use add-ons with Google Meet (Android)

Use add-ons with Google Meet

On your computer or mobile device, you can use Google Meet add-ons to enhance collaboration, productivity, and the overall experience of your meetings.

Tip: For Meet users who have a Workspace admin, your admin may pre-install or restrict the usage of certain add-ons for you. Learn how admins can control your add-ons experience.

All users will find pre-installed 1P apps from Google by default on their device.

Eligibility

You can’t use add-ons if:

  • Your Workspace admin has blocked the add-on.
  • You use Meet through a Family Link account.
  • Your meeting host has assigned you a View only role.
  • You’re not signed in with a Google Account.
  • You’re under the age of consent in your country or region.
  • You are in a client-side encrypted meeting or attending a Live Stream event.
About third-party add-ons

  • If you use Google Meet with an enterprise or education account: Add-ons are available for all meetings and calls regardless of the number of participants.

  • If you use Google Meet with a personal account: Add-ons are available for all meetings regardless of the number of participants. Tip: All add-ons don’t work across every platform.

  • When you’re on an unsupported platform, you’ll get this pop-up notification: “Can’t join the activity.”

  • If you have an add-on installed on a desktop that doesn’t work on a mobile device, the system will gray it out in the Tools panel and list it as an unavailable add-on.

Install third-party add-ons within Google Meet
  • To make call controls appear, tap the screen More controls Tools .
  • In the “Tools” tab, there’s a list of featured add-ons you can install:
    • Kahoot
    • Samsung Notes
    • Spotify
      • Important: Only Consumer users can see this add-on, not Enterprise users.
  • Tip: Within the Tools section, you can install Spotify directly.
  • If you want to install an add-on, tap its icon.
  • From the new screen, tap Install the add-on.
    • If the add-on you want to use isn’t listed as a featured add-on:
      • At the bottom of the “Tools tab,” tap Add .
      • Search for the add-on you want to use.
  • At the top right of the listing page, tap Install.
  • From the new screen, tap the Google account you used to join the meeting.
  • To download the add-on, sign in.
  • Tap Continue.
  • To provide the add-on access to your Google account, scroll to review permissions.
  • Tap Allow Done.
    • After you install the add-on from the Workspace Marketplace, download the add-on app from the Google Play Store.
      • If the add-on app is already installed, you can skip the steps below.
  • Re-open the Meet app .
  • To access call controls, tap the screen More controls Tools .
  • Tap the add-on you want to install.
    • Or, you can search for the add-on from the Marketplace.
  • Tap Install the app.
  • In the Google Play Store page of the add-on, tap Install.
  • After installation, you can use the third-party add-on for collaboration within Google Meet.
Use other Google products as add-ons within Google Meet

You can use certain Google products such as YouTube as add-ons within Google Meet to enhance the overall experience of your meetings.

Google products that are available as add-ons are built into the Meet app. To use them within Google Meet you’ll need to Install the Google app from the Play Store (if it’s not pre-installed).

To Install the Google app from the Play Store (if it’s not pre-installed):

  • In the Meet app , tap the screen so that call controls appear.
  • Tap More controls Tools .
  • In the “Tools tab,” under the Google section, you’ll notice a list of Google products.
  • Tap a Google product you want to collaborate with.
  • Tap Install.
  • From the Google Play Store page, tap Install.
  • To use the Google add-on for collaboration with other meeting attendees, after installation, go back to the Meet app . Tip: Once you start an activity with a Google add-on, you may be asked to read and accept the Terms of Service of the particular Google app. Follow the on-screen instructions if prompted. You’ll only be required to accept the Terms of Service once.
For Meeting Hosts
Start an activity with an add-on

Important: Make sure the add-on is installed and available (refer the sections above)

  • In the Meet app , tap the screen so that call controls appear.
  • Tap More controls Tools .
  • From the “Tools tab,” tap the add-on you want to collaborate with.
  • From the new screen, tap Open app.
  • On the add-on app you open, select the content or video you want to share.
  • You’ll notice an on-screen prompt to “Start a Meet Activity.”
  • Tap Start.
  • Once the activity begins, other meeting participants will be able to join the activity with you Important: Previously, some Google Meet users might have used the Meet app to play games or co-watch videos. These experiences were pre-built into the Meet app and didn’t require any additional installation. These experiences will continue to be available but will now require installing them as add-ons (refer steps to install add-ons above). Keep in mind that not all experiences will move over right away.
End an activity
  • From the blue banner on top of your screen, tap End.
  • From the on-screen pop-up, tap End activity. Important: If a meeting host leaves the meeting, the activity automatically ends for all the participants.
For Meeting Participants
Join an activity with an add-on

Joining an activity when you already have the add-on installed

  • Join the meeting.

  • At the top of your screen, on the blue banner, tap Join. Joining an activity when you don’t have the add-on installed

  • Join the meeting.

  • At the top of your screen, you’ll notice a blue banner with the name of the add-on you currently use.

  • Tap Get the app or Get the add-on.

  • Tip: This depends on the kind of add-on a host has started an activity with.

  • If it’s a third party add-on: Refer to the “Install third party add-ons within Google Meet” section above to complete the installation process.

    • After installation, go back to the Meet app .
    • From the blue banner at the top of the Meet screen, tap Join.

  • If it’s a Google product add-on: Refer to the “Use other Google products as add-ons within Google Meet” section above to complete the installation process.

    • After installation, go back to the Meet app .
    • From the blue banner at the top, tap Join. Tip: In some cases an add-on might not be eligible to use. This can be due to reasons such as an add-on being disallowed by your admin, add-on not compatible with your device, and so on. When this happens, you’ll notice a “Can’t join activity” prompt on your screen. To dismiss, tap Got it.
Leave an activity
  • From the blue banner at the top of your Meet screen, tap Leave Activity.
  • From the pop-up that appears, tap Leave Activity. When you leave an activity, other meeting participants might still continue to collaborate via the add-on until the meeting host ends the activity for everyone.

If you want to return to the activity after leaving it, from the blue banner at the top of screen, tap Join.

Tip: Hosts also have the ability to end the activity for all participants.

Learn about host controls

This is currently available on desktop. If a non-host joins from a mobile device, they won’t be able to start an add-on activity.

  • You use Meet with a Family Link account. If you use a Family Link account, you can’t install add-ons.

Leave an activity

Important: When you leave an activity, you’ll be sent back to the meeting. Hosts can also end an activity for all participants.

  • At the bottom right, click Tools .
  • Click Active add-on Leave activity.
Start an activity with a third-party add-on

All meeting participants can start add-on activities by default. Meeting hosts can choose to disallow other participants from starting an add-on activity. If you click an add-on and see an on-screen notification that says “You can’t use this add-on with others. Only a host can share add-on activities in this meeting.” it means that the host has currently disallowed you to use this feature.

  • While in a meeting, at the bottom right, click Tools .
  • Click the add-on you want to use.
  • Based on the add-on you select, follow the conditional steps:
    • Depending on the third-party add-on you select, you’ll either be asked to sign in to the add-on app through your Google Account or you’ll be able to proceed without signing in. If the add-on app requires you to sign in, then follow the on-screen prompts to sign in to the third-party app.
    • Depending on the add-on, you’ll notice a new screen within the add-ons panel which will require you to select or input a few options.
      • Example: At this step, you can select a specific file to collaborate on with others.
    • Depending on the add-on, you may be required to share file access with other meeting guests. To give access, follow on-screen prompts.
  • After you complete the conditional steps, click your activity will begin.
  • When the pop-up message “Others who have the add-on installed can interact with the content on their main screen” appears, click Continue.
    • Other meeting participants can now collaborate with you while using the third-party add-on in Meet.
  • Optional but recommended: To make sure that participants who don’t have the add-on can observe the activity:
    • When an activity starts, on the banner, at the top of the ongoing add-on activity, click Screen share Allow.
  • To end the activity, on the banner, at the top of the ongoing add-on activity, click End activity. Tip: You can only collaborate on one add-on at a time.

Computer AndroidiPhone & iPad

Use add-ons with Google Meet (iPhone and iPad)

Use add-ons with Google Meet

On your computer or mobile device, you can use Google Meet add-ons to enhance collaboration, productivity, and the overall experience of your meetings.

Tip: For Meet users who have a Workspace admin, your admin may pre-install or restrict the usage of certain add-ons for you. Learn how admins can control your add-ons experience.

All users will find pre-installed 1P apps from Google by default on their device.

Eligibility

You can’t use add-ons if:

  • Your Workspace admin has blocked the add-on.
  • You use Meet through a Family Link account.
  • Your meeting host has assigned you a View only role.
  • You’re not signed in with a Google Account.
  • You’re under the age of consent in your country or region.
  • You are in a client-side encrypted meeting or attending a Live Stream event.
About third-party add-ons

  • If you use Google Meet with an enterprise or education account: Add-ons are available for all meetings and calls regardless of the number of participants.

  • If you use Google Meet with a personal account: Add-ons are available for all meetings regardless of the number of participants. Tip: All add-ons don’t work across every platform.

  • When you’re on an unsupported platform, you’ll get this pop-up notification: “Can’t join the activity.”

  • If you have an add-on installed on a desktop that doesn’t work on a mobile device, the system will gray it out in the Tools panel and list it as an unavailable add-on.

Install third-party add-ons within Google Meet
  • To make call controls appear, tap the screen More controls Tools .
  • In the “Tools” tab, you can install featured add-ons like Spotify.
    • Important: Only Consumer users can see this add-on, not Enterprise users. Tip: Within the Tools section, you can install Spotify directly.
  • If you want to install an add-on, tap its icon.
  • From the new screen, tap Install the add-on.
  • Tap Install the app.
  • In the App Store page of the add-on, tap Install.
  • After installation, you can use the third-party add-on for collaboration within Google Meet.
Use other Google products as add-ons within Google Meet

You can use certain Google products such as YouTube as add-ons within Google Meet to enhance the overall experience of your meetings.

Google products that are available as add-ons are built into the Meet app. To use them within Google Meet you’ll need to Install the Google app from the Play Store (if it’s not pre-installed).

To Install the Google app from the Play Store (if it’s not pre-installed):

  • In the Meet app , tap the screen so that call controls appear.
  • Tap More controls Tools .
  • In the “Tools tab,” under the Google section, you’ll notice a list of Google products.
  • Tap a Google product you want to collaborate with.
  • Tap Install.
  • From the Google Play Store page, tap Install.
  • To use the Google add-on for collaboration with other meeting attendees, after installation, go back to the Meet app . Tip: Once you start an activity with a Google add-on, you may be asked to read and accept the Terms of Service of the particular Google app. Follow the on-screen instructions if prompted. You’ll only be required to accept the Terms of Service once.
For Meeting Hosts
Start an activity with an add-on

Important: Make sure the add-on is installed and available (refer the sections above)

  • In the Meet app , tap the screen so that call controls appear.
  • Tap More controls Tools .
  • From the “Tools tab,” tap the add-on you want to collaborate with.
  • From the new screen, tap Open app.
  • On the add-on app you open, select the content or video you want to share.
  • You’ll notice an on-screen prompt to “Start a Meet Activity.”
  • Tap Start.
  • Once the activity begins, other meeting participants will be able to join the activity with you Important: Previously, some Google Meet users might have used the Meet app to play games or co-watch videos. These experiences were pre-built into the Meet app and didn’t require any additional installation. These experiences will continue to be available but will now require installing them as add-ons (refer steps to install add-ons above). Keep in mind that not all experiences will move over right away.
End an activity
  • From the blue banner on top of your screen, tap End.
  • From the on-screen pop-up, tap End activity. Important: If a meeting host leaves the meeting, the activity automatically ends for all the participants.
For Meeting Participants
Join an activity with an add-on

Joining an activity when you already have the add-on installed

  • Join the meeting.

  • At the top of your screen, on the blue banner, tap Join. Joining an activity when you don’t have the add-on installed

  • Join the meeting.

  • At the top of your screen, you’ll notice a blue banner with the name of the add-on you currently use.

  • Tap Get the app or Get the add-on.

  • Tip: This depends on the kind of add-on a host has started an activity with.

  • If it’s a third party add-on: Refer to the “Install third party add-ons within Google Meet” section above to complete the installation process.

    • After installation, go back to the Meet app .
    • From the blue banner at the top of the Meet screen, tap Join.

  • If it’s a Google product add-on: Refer to the “Use other Google products as add-ons within Google Meet” section above to complete the installation process.

    • After installation, go back to the Meet app .
    • From the blue banner at the top, tap Join. Tip: In some cases an add-on might not be eligible to use. This can be due to reasons such as an add-on being disallowed by your admin, add-on not compatible with your device, and so on. When this happens, you’ll notice a “Can’t join activity” prompt on your screen. To dismiss, tap Got it.
Leave an activity
  • From the blue banner at the top of your Meet screen, tap Leave Activity.
  • From the pop-up that appears, tap Leave Activity. When you leave an activity, other meeting participants might still continue to collaborate via the add-on until the meeting host ends the activity for everyone.

If you want to return to the activity after leaving it, from the blue banner at the top of screen, tap Join.

Tip: Hosts also have the ability to end the activity for all participants.

Learn about host controls

This is currently available on desktop. If a non-host joins from a mobile device, they won’t be able to start an add-on activity.

iPhone & iPad AndroidComputer

Join a video meeting

Join a meeting

Join a meeting

You can join a video meeting from Google Meet, Google Calendar, or Gmail.

To join a meeting, you can also:

  • Use meeting links
  • Dial-in with a phone
  • Use Google meeting rooms or third-party devices
  • Join without a Google Account
  • Use On-the-Go mode Learn which meetings you can join

Account type

Meetings you can join

Personal account, Google One, or Google Workspace Individual

Any meetings organized by personal account, Google One, or Google Workspace Individual users.

Some meetings organized by other Google Workspace users.

Tip: Certain Workspace admins can restrict your access to their meetings.

Google Workspace for Education

By default, any meetings organized by Google Workspace users. This excludes Workspace Individual users.

Your Google Workspace admin controls what meetings you can join and can change this to:

  • Only join meetings organized by someone in your school.
  • Join meetings organized by anyone. Google Workspace

By default, any meetings organized by personal account, Google One, Google Workspace, or Google Workspace Individual users.

Your Google Workspace admin controls what meetings you can join and can change this to:

  • Only join meetings organized by someone in your organization.
  • Only join meetings organized by Google Workspace users. This doesn’t include Workspace Individual subscribers. Learn who can join your meetings

Account type

Who can join your meetings

Personal account, Google One, or Google Workspace Individual

All Google Account users.

Tips:

  • Some Workspace admins might stop their users from joining the meetings you organize.
  • Users who haven’t signed in to a Google Account must request to join.
  • If you’re a Workspace Individual user, people who dial-in by phone can also join your meetings. Google Workspace for Education

By default, only users in your school and anyone who dial-in with a phone.

Your admin can change this to:

  • Anyone signed in with a Google Account or those who dial-in with a phone.
  • Everyone, even users not signed in with a Google Account. Google Workspace

By default, all Google Account users and those who haven’t signed in to a Google Account.

Your admin can change this to:

  • Only users in your organization or anyone who dial-in with a phone.
  • Anyone signed in with a Google Account.
  • Everyone, even users not signed in with a Google Account.
Join a video meeting from Google Meet

In Google Meet, to join a video meeting:

  • On your computer, go to meet.google.com.

  • Select a meeting from your list of scheduled events.

    • Or, use a meeting code or nickname:
      • Enter the meeting code or nickname.
      • Click Join.

  • In the window that opens, click Join now. Tips:

  • When the first 5 participants join, you can hear a chime sound. After that, you get a silent notification for new participants.

  • You can only use meeting nicknames with people in your organization. This is currently available only to Google Workspace users.

Learn about other ways to join a meeting

Join a video meeting from a Google Calendar event

How to: Join Google Meet from Google Calendar using Google Workspace for business

You can find your scheduled meetings in Calendar and join a video meeting.

  • On your computer, go to Google Calendar.
  • Select the event.
  • Click Join with Google Meet.
  • In the window that opens, click Join now. If your Google Workspace admin allows it, you can also join from other video meeting devices.

Join a video meeting from Gmail

Learn how to join a meeting from Gmail.

Join a video meeting with a meeting link URL

If you don’t have enough time to schedule a meeting or book a room, you can join a video meeting with a link.

  • Open the chat message or email with the meeting link.
  • Click the meeting link.
  • In the window that opens, click Join now. Tip: If you’re not on the calendar invite, you need to request to join and the meeting organizer or a participant must let you in.

Use a phone to dial-in

Important:

  • You can only dial-in if the meeting is organized by a Google Workspace user.
  • A dial-in number is only added when admins turn on the dial-in feature. If your Google Workspace admin allows it, you can call in for audio-only access from 15 minutes before the meeting starts until it ends. Someone in the meeting can let you in sooner.

You can be from a different organization or use a different Google Workspace edition than the event organizer. If you’re in the organizer’s directory, your name shows in the meeting. If not, it shows as “Private caller.”

  • Participants should always verify the identity of callers.
  • Anyone who calls in counts toward the maximum participant limit.
  • Regular call charges apply. Tip: When the first 5 participants join, you can hear a chime sound. After that, you get a silent notification for new participants.
Dial-in with a phone number

Important:

  • If you try to call into a meeting before it starts, you might get an error that the PIN isn’t recognized.

  • For the list of supported countries or regions, refer to countries where you can use a phone with Meet.

  • In the Meet or Calendar app, tap the dial-in number.

    • Or, you can:
      • Dial the number shown in the Google Calendar event or meeting invitation.
      • Enter the PIN, followed by “#”.

  • To mute or unmute, press *6. Tips:

  • All Google Workspace editions include a US phone number.

  • These Google Workspace editions support international numbers in video meetings:

    • G Suite Basic
    • G Suite Business
    • Google Workspace Essentials
    • Enterprise
    • Education Plus

  • If your organization turns on “Meet Global Dialing,” additional international numbers become available.

  • Long distance and usage charges from your phone carrier may apply. Use a Google meeting room or third-party device

Use Google Meet hardware

To join a meeting, select the event from the list of scheduled events.

  • Or, use the meeting code or nickname. Learn more about Google Meet hardware.
Use third-party devices

If your organization allows it, you can join meetings from third-party devices. If you’re an admin, learn how to allow 3rd party devices.

If you use a Zoom Rooms or Cisco Webex device:

To join a meeting, select the event from the list of scheduled events.

  • Or, use the meeting code or nickname.

    • On your meeting device, open the Google Meet app .
    • Enter the meeting code. If you use other third-party devices with Pexip:

  • On your computer, go to Google Calendar.

  • Select the event you want to join.

  • Click Other ways to join Third-party systems.

  • Follow the on-screen instructions. Tip: If you join from a third-party device:

  • You must use the third-party controls. Without third-party controls, you can’t use features like:

    • Turn your camera or microphone on or off
    • Meeting chat
    • Record meetings
    • Admit or remove other participants
    • Mute or unmute other participants

  • Other Meet participants can’t mute your room. Join without a Google Account

You can join a meeting without a Google Account, but the organizer or a participant needs to let you in.

  • On your computer, to join a meeting:
    • With a meeting link:
      • Open the chat message or email with the meeting link.
      • Click the meeting link.
    • From Google Meet:
      • Go to meet.google.com.
      • Click Enter code.
      • Enter the meeting code.
      • Click Join.
  • Enter your name.
  • Click Ask to join. Join a video meeting On-the-Go

Learn how to use On-the-Go mode for meetings.

Learn about meeting privacy
  • When you join a meeting, to fix issues and for audit purposes, we share your meeting identifiers, like email or phone number with the host.
  • If you use a personal Google Account and when a user flagged for bad behavior joins the meeting, the moderator gets a message. The message shows “This person is suspected of being bad in the past.”

Use Connect room feature in Google Meet

Use Connect room feature in Google Meet

With the “Connect room” feature, you can easily and quickly start meetings inside Google Meet rooms from your laptop. This feature saves time and simplifies the process to join and start meetings.

Start a meeting with “Connect room”

Important: To access the “Connect room” feature, your Workspace admin must first turn on the Proximity Detection device setting in the Admin Console. Learn how to turn proximity on or off for Meet hardware devices.

To use the “Connect room” feature:

  • Enter a Google Meet Hardware enabled conference room.
  • On your laptop, go to Google Meet.
  • On the Meet page, you can either:
    • Enter a code or nickname click Join.
    • Select a scheduled meeting.
  • It re-directs you to the pre-meeting screen, also known as the green room. Once in the green room, on the right side of your screen, the “Use Companion mode” button changes to “Room detected” and then transitions to “Connect Room.”
    • Important: When you click ”Connect a Room,” you join the meeting both on your laptop through Companion mode and in the conference room. Companion mode preserves your current camera status, whether it’s off or on. The conference room automatically turns on its camera and microphone.
  • Click Connect room.
    • You directly join the meeting via the Google Meet Hardware device and your laptop automatically checks into the room through Companion Mode.
    • When you’re in Companion Mode, you can:
      • Use Meet features that aren’t available through the Meet Hardware device. This includes features like Q&A and Polling.
      • Make your presence easily recognizable when multiple people join a meeting from the same room. Learn how to use Companion mode for better collaboration. Tips:
  • Make sure your laptop isn’t connected to an external microphone or a bluetooth device. Otherwise, your laptop can’t detect the ultrasound needed to connect with a room.
  • The “Connect room” feature relies on ultrasound signals. Individuals or animals with sensitive hearing may hear these tones. In these cases, you can:
    • Temporarily turn off this feature at a device level through the Google Meet touch controller. After the meeting ends, this feature automatically turns on. To turn off this feature:
      • On the Meet Hardware device, tap More Detection.
      • Turn off Proximity.
    • Turn off this feature for your entire organization. This also turns off Proximity Detection. Learn how to turn proximity on or off for Meet hardware devices.
  • If you use “Connect room” to join a meeting that’s recorded, transcribed, and/or where Gemini is taking notes, you automatically consent to use these features.
Use a room code if the “Connect room” button doesn’t appear

If the “Connect room” button doesn’t appear as expected, you can connect using a room code.

Important: This feature is currently only available if your organization is in the Google Meet Hardware Early Preview Rooms Program and on the Workspace Rapid Release track. Your Workspace admin must opt your organization into both of these two options.

  • Enter a Google Meet Hardware enabled conference room.
  • On your laptop, go to Google Meet.
  • On the Meet page, you can either:
    • Enter a meeting code or nickname click Join.
    • Select a scheduled meeting.
  • You’ll be redirected to the pre-meeting screen, also known as the green room.
  • On the right side of your laptop’s screen, click Connect with room code.
  • Find the room code at the top of the main device screen in the conference room. “Room code:” appears before the code.
  • On your laptop, enter the room code, then click Connect room.
  • Tap Connect on the meeting touch screen to confirm you are inside the room.
Meeting scenarios for “Connect room” feature

You can start hassle-free meetings in different situations with “Connect room.” These situations include but aren’t limited to:

  • Take over a booked, but empty conference room: If a conference room is reserved but unoccupied, open your meeting on your laptop, click ‘Connect room’, and you can immediately start your meeting on the Google Meet hardware.
  • Join and book an available conference room in one click: If you find an available and bookable conference room and wish to use it, simply open your meeting on your laptop, click ‘Connect room’, and the Google Meet hardware will instantly join the meeting, simultaneously booking the room for your use.
  • Join private meetings more easily: Simply open a meeting invite on your device, click ‘Connect room’, and instantly join the meeting directly on Google Meet hardware.
  • Join a meeting not listed on the conference room calendar: If you were sent a Google Meet invitation in chat or email, open your meeting on your laptop, click ‘Connect room’, and you can immediately start your meeting on the Google Meet hardware.
FAQ’s

Why can’t I find the “Connect room” button?

There are a few reasons why this could happen:

  • It’s available for laptop or desktop users only. It’s not available on mobile and tablet devices.
  • It’s currently only available for users on a Google Chrome browser.
  • It’s for a Meet green room only and you must be on the page. This feature doesn’t work on g.co/present or g.co/companion.
  • The laptop’s microphone isn’t selected. If you have multiple microphones, Proximity Detection only uses the currently selected microphone.
    • If you use a USB headset or dongle as your mic, it may cause Proximity Detection to fail. This can happen if:
      • The microphone’s range is limited.
      • The microphone’s audio processing filters out ultrasonic sound.
      • The headset is off.
  • Proximity Detection doesn’t work if:
    • You try to join a meeting through g.co/present or g.co/companion.
    • Your laptop is configured to filter out the ultrasound frequency. To check if you filter anything out:
      • For Chrome OS users: Turn off studio-style mic or noise cancellation.
      • For Windows users: On your laptop audio device, disable audio enhancements.
      • For Mac OS users: Turn off voice isolation. I hear a high-pitched noise. How can I disable this feature in my conference room?

You can temporarily disable this feature through the touch controller, before or during a meeting. After the meeting ends, this feature automatically turns on again.

To disable this feature:

  • On the Meet Hardware device, tap More Detection.
  • Turn off Proximity. Why can’t I use “Connect room” for my meeting?

“Connect room” doesn’t start the following meeting types on conference room hardware:

  • Meet Live

  • Meet Client-side encryption The tooltip of the “Connect room” button shows “Multiple rooms found. Close nearby doors and check for other nearby Meet devices.” I have closed the door of the room I am in, but it is still showing that, what should I do?

  • Wait a few seconds. The tooltip changes to show the room name you’re connecting to once it stops receiving signals from other rooms.

  • Check if there are multiple Google Meet Hardware devices in your room. If yes, you can turn off Proximity Detection on the rest of the devices except for the main device. This will allow you to connect your laptop with the main hardware device. To turn off Proximity Detection on the incorrect devices:

    • On the Meet Hardware device, tap More Detection.
    • Turn off Proximity. I see the “Connect room” button when I join meetings from my desk. What is happening and why?

Your laptop picks up an ultrasonic signal from a nearby conference room device. You can disregard the button. To join the call from your laptop, click Join now.

Will “Connect room” book a room for me so I don’t get kicked out?

Yes, it will if you use “Connect room” in an available conference room with in-room bookings. This booking lasts up to:

  • 30 minutes
  • The duration of your scheduled meeting, if the room is available the entire time.
  • Whatever time is available until its next booking. Tip: You can join a meeting with “Connect room” that’s already booked for another meeting. However, the room isn’t automatically released or booked for your meeting.

Resolve known issues

A future update will address the following known issues.

The Google Meet Series One Audiobar speaker might not play sound in a meeting.

To resolve this:

  • Reboot the device.
  • Contact Google Workspace support. If the issue persists, on your device, turn off Proximity Detection.

Tip: If multiple rooms are detected, Google Meet may start the meeting on the wrong conference room device.
