Learn how Dual Screen on Google Meet works

Learn how Dual Screen on Google Meet works

On a Google Meet call, you can turn on your front and back selfie cameras at the same time. When you turn on both cameras, other meeting participants can see you and other people around you at the same time.

Tips:

  • This feature is only available on the Google Pixel 9 Pro Fold device.
  • Make sure to keep your Meet and Gmail app updated while using this feature.
Use Dual Camera & Dual Display with Google Meet
  • On your Google Pixel 9 Pro Fold device, in the Meet or Gmail app, join or create a meeting.
  • On the Meet call, tap anywhere outside your floating self-view picture.
  • In the call controls that show on your floating self-view picture, tap Turn on dual camera .
    • Tip: Once you enable dual camera, dual display is automatically enabled.
  • To turn off both “Dual Camera” and “Dual Display,” tap on your floating self-view picture tap Turn off dual camera .
  • Optional: To only turn off “Dual Display,” at the top right of your call screen, tap Turn off other screen .

Learn how Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Meet & Vids protects your data

Learn how Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Meet & Vids protects your data

Across Google and Workspace, we’ve long shared robust privacy commitments that outline how we protect user data and prioritize privacy. Generative AI doesn’t change these commitments — it actually reaffirms their importance.

Our privacy commitments to all Workspace users

Generative AI does not change our foundational privacy protections for giving users choice and control over their data. To that end, here are key facts about how Workspace data is handled.

  • Your data is your data. The content that you put into Google Workspace services (emails, documents, etc.) is yours. We never sell your data, and you can delete your content or export it.
  • Your data stays in Workspace. We do not use your Workspace data to train or improve the underlying generative AI and large language models that power Gemini, Search, and other systems outside of Workspace without permission.
  • Your privacy is protected. Interactions with intelligent Workspace features, such as accepting or rejecting spelling suggestions, or reporting spam, are anonymized and/or aggregated and may be used to improve or develop helpful Workspace features like spam protection, spell check, and autocomplete. These Workspace features are developed with strict privacy protections that keep users in control.
  • Your content is not used for ads targeting. As a reminder, Google does not collect, scan, or use your content in Google Workspace services for advertising purposes. Important: If you’re a Workspace user with a personal account and you choose to share data, including your Workspace data, with Gemini Apps or Search services for Personal Intelligence, or through screen actions (including screenshots), this data will be processed according to their respective terms and policies, and may be used for model training and improvement. Learn more in the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub or the Search services Frequently Asked Questions.

These are the privacy commitments that Workspace extends to all of its users. But they aren’t just words. To ensure we continually meet these high standards, independent auditors validate our practices against international standards and best practices.

Specific commitments for Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet & Vids

For users with Google AI plans, when using Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Meet, and Vids, your data is yours and under your control. Whether you ask Gemini to summarize an email or document, write a blog post, or add a unique image to your slide:

  • Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, and Vids uses your content in Google Workspace to provide more useful responses to your prompts and doesn’t use your content to train or improve Gemini or other generative AI models.
  • Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, and Vids doesn’t store your prompt or the generated output without your permission. Note: For users enrolled in the Google Workspace Experiments program, use of Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Vids, and Meet is covered by the Google Workspace Experiments Privacy Notice & Terms for Personal Accounts.

Learn how to use Chat with Google Meet

Learn how to use Chat with Google Meet

With continuous meeting chat, you can send messages to meeting participants before, during and after a meeting in Google Chat. Continuous meeting chat is available to all Business and Enterprise users.

  • If continuous meeting chat is enabled: You can use additional Google Chat features such as text formatting, @mentions, and reactions. Your messages sync with Google Chat, and you can access the meeting chat before, during, and after the meeting.

    • If you’re a guest from outside the host’s organization, or not signed in, messages are only available while you are in the meeting. When the meeting ends, all your messages disappear.

  • If continuous meeting chat is disabled or not available: Messages are only available while you are in the call and disappear as soon as the meeting ends. Learn more about the chat experience with continuous meeting chat disabled. If you join a meeting on the web:

  • Internal guests on the Google Calendar Invite: Your conversations are saved in your Chat conversations list and you can access the entire chat history of a meeting, even if you join late.

  • Internal guests who aren’t on the Calendar invite and guests from outside the host’s organization: Your chat history disappears when the meeting ends and you can only access messages while you’re in the meeting. If you join a meeting on a mobile device:

  • Internal guests on the Google Calendar invite: You’ll be directed to the Google Chat app or Gmail app to send or read a chat message in a Google Meet event. The conversation is saved in your Chat conversations list, and you can access the entire chat history of a meeting, even if you join late. You’ll also have access to all rich features like @mentions and reactions.

  • Internal guests who aren’t on the Calendar invite and guests from outside the host’s organization: Your chat history disappears when the meeting ends, and you can only access messages that are sent during the time you’re in the meeting. However, internal guests who were included on the Calendar invite will be able to view chats sent during the meeting, even after the meeting.

Learn who can use continuous meeting chat

You can use continuous meeting chat in Google Meet with these Google Workspace editions:

  • Enterprise Essentials, Enterprise Essentials Plus
  • Enterprise Starter, Enterprise Standard, Enterprise Plus
  • Business Starter, Business Standard, Business Plus
  • Frontline Starter, Frontline Standard, Frontline Plus
Understand why continuous meeting chat is unavailable

Important: If you can’t use continuous chat in Meet, you still have access to Meet’s in-meeting chat.

Continuous meeting chat allows participants to communicate through Google Chat before, during, and after a meeting.

If continuous meeting chat is enabled:

  • You can’t set up a live stream in the meeting.

  • Chat messages aren’t saved to the organizer’s drive with the recording of the meeting.

  • Viewers can send chat messages. If chat is limited to in-meeting, it stops when the call ends. If a participant only has the in-meeting experience, this can be because of:

  • Meeting type

  • Host configuration

  • User or device limitation

  • Organization or policy restriction

  • Workspace admin settings

Learn about meetings & configuration

Certain meeting types or host configurations don’t support continuous meeting chats:

  • Meeting types:
    • Live streams
    • Instant meetings
    • Client Side Encryption (CSE) meetings
    • Breakout rooms
    • Meetings with waiting rooms
    • Huddles
    • Events without a Meet ID
  • Conference types: Messages in Breakout rooms or when Waiting room is enabled.
  • Disabled chats: An administrator can disable Google Chat service for specific users.
  • Host controls: If a host turns off chat in the Calendar event’s call option before the meeting, the host can’t change the setting until the meeting ends.
  • Guest list visibility: The meeting organizer turned off the “See guest list” setting for the event in Calendar.
  • Meeting size: Participants can only use continuous meeting chat for new meetings created in Google Calendar with up to 200 invited guests, including Google Groups.
  • Meetings with encryption: The meeting uses CSE in Meet settings. Tip: All messages follow your organization’s Google Chat retention policies. Learn how to retain Google Chat messages in Vault.
Learn about user & device limitations

These specific participants or devices may be restricted from access to the full chat history:

  • User type:
    • Drop-in or temporary users: Users with short-term, non-permanent access.
    • External or non-Workspace users: Users outside host organizations who need temporary or limited access.
    • Anonymous endpoints: Users who don’t sign in and can only access public content.
  • Hardware & software:
    • Devices: Endpoints such as Zoom Rooms or Cisco Webex Rooms.
    • Mobile: Devices with an outdated operating system, an old version of the Chat app, or no Chat app installed.
    • Accessibility: If you use Voice Over software, you get a sound notification when you get a message but the message isn’t voiced over. To hear the message, open the chat panel.
Learn about organization & policy restrictions

Administrative settings on your domain or another participant’s domain can restrict functionality with:

  • External chat policies: If an organizer’s domain prohibits chats with external users, guests outside the organization can’t send messages.
  • Chat history: To use continuous chat, turn on History. If a user’s policy forces “Chat history off” while the meeting requires “Chat history on,” that user gets a view-only experience. They can read messages but can’t reply.
  • Invited guests: If their admin disables Google chat for invited guests, the meeting won’t support continuous meeting chat.
Manage meeting conversations in Google Chat

To help you organize your meeting chats, you can have your meeting conversations added automatically to a dedicated “Meeting” section in Google Chat.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • In the left panel, find the “Direct messages” section.
  • Next to “Direct messages,” click Section actions Create meeting section .
  • In the pop-up message, click Create.
Start a new Meeting Conversation

A Meeting Conversation can be created by selecting “Chat with Guests” from a Calendar invite, accessing the group chat within your Chat list of conversations, or by sending the first message using the embedded chat in Meet.

For recurring events in Calendar, a separate Meeting Conversation is created for each individual instance and is located under the “Direct Messages” section of your Chat conversations list.

The Meeting Conversation name will combine the event name and date. For example, “Sales Team Weekly - Nov 8” and “Sales Team Weekly - Nov 15.” The date in the title uses the format and language of your current language settings in your account. Learn more about how to change your language on the web.

Important:

  • External guests invited to a meeting via the “Chat with Guests” feature in Calendar aren’t automatically added to the Meeting Conversation.
  • A new Meeting Conversation won’t be created or displayed in your Chat conversations list if no message is sent before or during the meeting.
  • Meeting Conversations have the same retention policies as Google Chat spaces. Learn about message history for conversations with work or school accounts.
  • Meeting conversations (which are group direct messages) created via Meet or Calendar cannot be converted into Google Chat spaces.
  • External guests will only have access to the chat during the time they are in the meeting. They will not see the conversation history from before or after they join. Internal attendees will see clear ‘external’ indicators and banners when guests are present in the conversation. There will be an external warning in the header of chat and a compose warning.
Send a chat message in a video meeting

How to send chat messages in a Google Meet meeting

On your computer
  • On your computer, join a Meet video meeting.
  • At the bottom right, click Chat .
  • Enter a message.
  • Click Send .
    • Messages are visible to everyone in the call and internal guests on the calendar invite, even if they’re not in the call).
    • Chat features such as text formatting, @mentions, and reactions are only available if continuous chat is on for Google Workspace Business or Enterprise users.
On your phone or tablet
  • On your device, join a Meet video meeting.
  • At the bottom, tap More controls Chat with everyone .
  • Enter a message.
  • Tap Send .
Learn how continuous meeting chat works if you’re outside the host’s organization or not on the calendar invite

When a meeting starts, messages sent in Google Chat are visible to all participants in the meeting. When the Google Meet call starts, a banner is displayed in Google Chat to notify users that the meeting associated with this chat is in-progress.

If you’re not part of the hosts organization, not signed in, or not on the calendar invite for the meeting, you can only:

  • Send messages to other participants while you’re in the meeting
  • Read messages sent by other participants after you join the meeting Additionally, when an external user joins the Google Meet call, all internal users are notified and an “External” badge is visible at all times in Google Chat.

Important: Messages sent before you join the meeting won’t be visible to you and you won’t see any messages after the meeting ends. Some rich media messages, such as images, video files, or custom domain GIFs, sent by internal users may be unavailable for external participants to view.

Learn how the Calendar event guest list affects meeting chats

As the event organizer, you control if people invited to your event can view the guest list. When you turn off “See guest list,” it affects how your meeting chat works.

  • If you turn off “See guest list” before the meeting chat is created:
    • “Chat with guests” isn’t available in the Calendar event for you or your guests.
    • Continuous meeting chat will not be available.
  • If you turn off “See guest list” after the meeting chat is created:
    • The chat continues to exist in Google Chat for its members.
    • The guest list in the chat no longer syncs with the guest list in the event.
      • For example, if you remove someone from the guest list in the event, it does not remove them from the chat. Prevent participants from sending chat messages in a video meeting

Important: To use this feature, you must turn on Host Management.

When continuous meeting chat is on, meeting hosts and organizers can stop participants from sending chat messages. Participants can still read the messages.

Turn chat messaging on or off during a meeting
On your computer
  • On your computer, join a Meet video meeting.
  • At the bottom right, click Host controls .
  • From the side panel that opens, turn Let contributors send messages on or off.
On your phone or tablet

  • On your device, join a Meet video meeting.

  • At the bottom, tap More controls Settings Host controls .

  • Turn Let contributors send messages on or off. Tips:

  • If you can’t turn the setting on or off, you might need to turn off a Chrome extension for Meet. Learn how to install and manage extensions.

  • If you turn chat messages off in a one-time, nicknamed, or instant meeting, the chat message setting turns back on after the meeting ends.

Turn chat messaging on or off before a Google Calendar scheduled meeting
  • Open Google Calendar.
  • Open an event.
  • Next to the Meet video link, click Video call options .
  • In the “Chat moderation,” section, turn Let contributors send messages on or off. Tip: If you turn chat messages off in recurring meetings or meetings that use the same meeting code, the setting is saved for the next scheduled meeting.
Manage chat for live stream viewers

Important: This is only available on iPhones and iPads.

Meeting hosts can:

  • Control chat messages for Google Meet live stream participants
  • Allow or prevent viewers from finding and sending chat messages
Control chat messages for live stream viewers
  • On your iPhone or iPad, join a Google Meet video meeting with an active live stream.
  • At the bottom, tap More controls Settings Host controls .
  • Under “Let live stream viewers,” turn these options on or off.
    • See chat messages: Control live stream viewers from finding chat messages.
    • Send chat messages: Control live stream viewers from sending chat messages.
Learn what hosts can let live stream viewers find
  • If a host turns “See chat messages” on or off, live stream viewers find a message that indicates:
    • Off: Chat is unavailable or off.
    • On: After viewers leave the call, they can’t access the messages.
  • If a host turns on “See chat messages” but turns off “Send chat messages:” Live stream viewers can find existing messages but can’t send new ones.
  • If a host turns on both “See chat messages” and “Send chat messages:” Live stream viewers can find and send messages.
Turn continuous meeting chat off

Before a scheduled meeting begins, continuous meeting chats are on by default. If you’re the meeting host and want to turn off continuous meeting chat, you can edit video call options within the Calendar event . After the meeting begins, this setting can’t be changed.

  • Open Google Calendar.
  • Open an event.
  • Next to the Meet video link, click Video call options .
  • In the “Chat moderation” section, select an option for Continuous meeting chat:
    • Off: Participants can send messages from the time they join the meeting. After the meeting ends, the messages disappear.
    • On: Participants in the same organization as the host can access their complete Google Chat history from before, during, and after the meeting.
Chat with others during a video meeting without continuous meeting chat

When continuous meeting chat is off, or the host doesn’t have the necessary requirements to use continuous meeting chat, you can only view and send messages from a computer or mobile device while you are in the meeting.

Important:

  • If you join a conference room using Google meeting room hardware, you can find the messages, but not send them.
  • Messages are visible to everyone in the call.
  • Except for pinned messages, you can only find the chat messages that are sent while you’re in a video meeting.
    • Messages that are sent before you join the meeting don’t display and all messages disappear when you leave.
    • Pinned messages aren’t available on mobile devices. If you join a meeting on your mobile device, the pinned messages don’t display.
  • If you use Meet with a Voice Over software, when a chat message is sent, you get a sound notification but the messages aren’t voiced over. To hear the message, open the chat panel.
  • When meetings are recorded the chat conversation log is also saved.
Pin a chat message during a video meeting

Important:

  • If you join a meeting with your computer: You can find pinned messages in the chat. This includes pinned messages that are created before you join the meeting.

  • If you join a meeting with your mobile device: The pinned messages don’t display.

  • You can pin and unpin your own messages. Hosts may unpin anyone’s messages. To pin a chat message:

  • On your computer, hover over a chat message.

  • At the top right, click Pin .

Present content from a camera in Google Meet

Present content from a camera in Google Meet

You can present live video from your camera in a Google Meet video meeting to showcase objects and create interactive presentations.

You can also connect to a document camera to share physical documents in a Google Meet.

Learn which Workspace editions can present from a camera

Important: You can present from a camera with these Workspace editions:

  • Business Standard
  • Business Plus
  • Enterprise Essentials
  • Enterprise Standard
  • Enterprise Plus
  • Education Plus
  • Teaching and Learning Upgrade
  • Google Workspace Individual
  • Frontline Standard
Turn on the present from a camera setting

Important:

  • If this setting isn’t enabled, you won’t be able to select a camera as a presentation option.
  • Make sure you’re connected to an additional video-conferencing or virtual camera.
  • Join a Google Meet video meeting.
  • At the bottom, click More options Settings General.
  • In the “General” tab, turn on Share content from camera.
    • If the computer plays audio that the microphone associated with the camera captures, enable “Use Meet’s audio signal processing for the audio associated with the camera content” to avoid an echo.
    • Recommended: If you’re not sure about how audio processing works, we recommend you to keep this option turned OFF.
  • At the top right of the dialogue box, click Close . You’ve now enabled the option to select a camera when you present.
Present from a camera during a video meeting

Important: Make sure you enable the present from a camera setting before you follow the instruction below:

  • In a video meeting, at the bottom of the meeting screen, click Present now Camera.
  • Select your document camera or other external camera and audio input (if necessary).
  • Click Share.
Ingest content from a video production tool

Important:

  • Make sure you enable the present from a camera setting before you follow the instruction below:
    • You can present live video from your video production tool.
  • This is recommended when you share a produced video material that has more dynamic content than the usual speaker webcam video.
  • The content is always uncropped, and encoded with resolution of up to 1080p, and a frame rate of up to 30FPS.
  • In a meeting invite, click Join.
  • In the greenroom, under “Other joining options,” click Use Companion mode.
  • At the bottom of the meeting screen, click Present now Camera.
  • Select your connected hardware device or virtual audio and video source.
  • Click Share.

Report a problem with Google Meet

Report a problem with Google Meet

Please provide feedback and share your ideas to help us improve Meet.

Tip: Additional details, such as web browser logs, are automatically included when you submit feedback. Your feedback enhances our ability to troubleshoot issues and improve Meet. Google Workspace administrators can turn off this feature. For details, see Client logs upload in Manage Meet settings.

In the meeting
  • Join a Google Meet meeting.
  • Click More .
  • Click Report a problem.
  • Describe the issue or share your ideas.
  • Select Include screenshot to help identify the issue.
  • Click Send.
After the meeting

Click Submit feedback when the video meeting ends.

Before a meeting
  • In a web browser, enter meet.google.com.
  • Click Support Report a problem.
  • Describe the issue or share your ideas.
  • Select Capture screenshot to help identify the issue or idea.
  • Click Send. You can also click the meeting link or calendar event. Before joining, click More and select Report a problem.

Computer AndroidiPhone & iPad

Report a problem with Google Meet (Android)

Report a problem with Google Meet

Please provide feedback and share your ideas to help us improve Meet.

Tip: Additional details, such as web browser logs, are automatically included when you submit feedback. Your feedback enhances our ability to troubleshoot issues and improve Meet. Google Workspace administrators can turn off this feature. For details, see Client logs upload in Manage Meet settings.

In the meeting
  • On your Android device, to show call controls when you’re in a meeting, tap the screen.
  • Tap More controls Settings .
  • Under “General,” tap Report a Problem Get Started.
    • You might get a one-time prompt that asks you to allow Google Play services to access all device logs. You can choose to allow one-time access or not.
  • Enter your issue.
  • Tap Send .
  • Meet takes a screenshot of your screen.
    • To delete the screenshot, tap Delete .
  • Tap Send feedback.
  • To close the “Send feedback” page, tap Close .
  • To return to the call screen, at the top left of the “Settings” page, tap Close .
Before a meeting
  • On your Android device, open the Meet app .
  • Tap Menu .
  • Tap Help & Feedback Send feedback Get Started.
    • You might get a one-time prompt that asks you to allow Google Play services to access all device logs. You can choose to allow one-time access or not.
  • Enter your issue.
  • Tap Send .
  • Meet takes a screenshot of your screen.
    • To delete the screenshot, tap Delete .
  • Tap Send feedback.
  • To close the “Send feedback” page, tap Close .
  • To return to the call screen, at the top left of the “Settings” page, tap Close .
Before or after a Meet legacy call

Learn more about Meet legacy calls.

  • Open Meet .
  • At the top left, tap More option .
  • Tap Help & feedback Send feedback.
  • Enter your comment or describe your problem.
    • Screenshot and logs: To help us understand the issue, you can include a screenshot and your app usage.
  • Tap Send .
Send feedback about a call

After you finish a call, you may be asked to rate the call as good or bad.

  • If you’re prompted, enter your rating.
  • If you rate a call as “bad,” let us know what the problem was. Some information about bad calls will automatically be sent to Google so we can understand the issue better. The info won’t include the call’s content.

Report abuse in a meeting

Report abuse in a meeting

As part of our commitment to keep meetings safe, you have the ability to report abuse from within Google Meet. You can report any participant who violates our Acceptable Use Policy. Once we receive your report, we’ll investigate it and take the appropriate action. We’ll get back to you only if we require additional details or have more information to share.

Report multiple participants simultaneously

Important: It’s mandatory to fill out all fields of the abuse form.

  • On the bottom of a meeting screen, click More options .
  • Click Report abuse .
  • In the pop-up box, select the abuse type.
  • Enter the display names of the abusers.
  • Describe the issue.
  • Click Report.
Attach a video clip when you report abuse

Important:

  • You can only attach a video clip to your abuse report in meetings organized by a consumer account user, i.e., someone who uses Meet with a non-Google Workspace subscriber account.

  • You can’t attach a video clip to your abuse report if a user with a Google Workspace subscriber account joins a meeting organized by a consumer account user. Some users might notice an optional checkbox that allows them to share a video clip of the meeting when they report abuse. The optional video clip:

  • Allows Google to understand the context behind an abusive meeting report. This includes:

    • Meeting disruption
    • Harassment
    • Child abuse, etc.

  • Exists to provide Google with more evidence of a potential violation of our Acceptable Use Policy. The video clip shared with Google:

  • Doesn’t include audio from the meeting

  • Isn’t more than one minute long

  • Is only used to validate abuse, which may include manual review, and is then deleted Computer AndroidiPhone & iPad

Report abuse in Gemini in Workspace apps

Report abuse in Gemini in Workspace apps

Important: This article only applies for reporting abuse about Gemini responses. For general feedback about Gemini responses, use Good suggestion or Bad suggestion . The terms in the feedback flow will apply when you submit general feedback.

If you get inaccurate or unsafe responses in Gemini in Workspace apps, you have the option to report them to us. Your feedback helps make Gemini in Workspace apps more helpful, accurate, and safe.

When you report a response, such as spam, fraud, or illegal content, your conversation with Gemini is added to your report, including:

  • Prompts

  • Context documents, emails, and other content

  • The response from Gemini To report abuse in Gemini in a Workspace app:

  • Next to a response, select the Report abuse option.

    • If you can’t find Report abuse, select More options .

  • Select the reason you wish to report content.

  • Click Report. Tip: You can also report a legal issue here.

Transfer a meeting between devices

Transfer a meeting between devices

You can join a meeting on Google Meet on one device and smoothly transfer it to another. This allows you to maintain an ongoing conversation without worrying about missing important information.

For example, if you commute to work and join a meeting on your mobile device, you can transfer the meeting to your computer at work to continue the conversation without the need to hang up or rejoin.

Transfer a meeting from mobile to your computer

Important: Learn how to join a meeting.

  • On your computer or laptop, open Google Meet.
  • Select the meeting you’re currently in.
  • Select Switch here. Tip: When you transfer the meeting, it disconnects from your original device. To stay in the meeting on both devices, under “Other joining options,” select Join here too.
Transfer a meeting between Android devices

Important: This feature is only available for Android devices that are versions 11 and up.

  • On your Android device, open Google Meet.
  • Join your meeting.
  • At the top right, tap Cast .
  • Select the device you’d like to transfer the meeting to.
    • If you don’t find the device you want to transfer the meeting to, learn how to set up cross-device services.
  • On the device you want to transfer the call to, tap Switch here. Tip: When you transfer the meeting, it disconnects from your original device. To stay in the meeting on both devices, under “Other joining options,” tap Join here too.

Troubleshoot camera issues in a meeting

Troubleshoot camera issues in a meeting

If you have a camera issue in a meeting, here’s how you can fix it:

  • Allow Google Meet to access your camera
  • Allow Google Chrome to access your camera
  • Allow camera access on a different browser other than Chrome
  • Allow your system or device to access your camera
  • Learn why you have a black screen or crossed out camera icon
Check your camera before your meeting
  • Make sure that your camera is connected, on, and faces towards you.
  • Choose the correct camera, not a screen or other devices. Learn how to connect your video and audio.
  • Test your camera in another app.
  • Close other apps that use the camera, then reload Meet.
  • Check your internet connection. Slow connections can cause video-quality problems. Learn how to improve your Wi-Fi or network performance.
  • Make sure your browser is updated.
    • Learn how to update Google Chrome.
    • Learn how to update Safari.
    • Learn how to update Firefox.
    • Learn how to update Microsoft Edge.
Allow camera access for Meet

You must allow camera access the first time you join a meeting.

  • On your computer, open meet.google.com.
  • Join a video meeting.
  • In the address bar, click Camera.
  • Turn on Camera.
  • Click Allow on every visit.
Allow camera access in Google Chrome
Check your site permissions

Important:

  • The “Camera failed” error often means your browser can’t access the camera.

  • You can allow all websites to use your camera or only a specific website. To allow your browser to use your camera:

  • On your computer, in the address bar, enter chrome://settings/content/camera.

  • Under “Default behavior,” select Sites can ask to use your camera.

  • Turn off Ask before accessing.

  • If you’ve allowed camera access for Meet before:

    • Under “Allowed to use your camera,” next to “meet.google.com:443,” click Delete.
    • Next to “meet.google.com:443,” click Expand .
    • Under “Permissions,” click Camera Allow Camera Access.
Allow camera access on other browsers
  • Allow Safari to use your camera.
  • Allow Firefox to use your camera.
  • Allow Microsoft Edge to use your camera.
Allow camera access on your computer or device

Important: Check that your camera is on and accessible by your computer and browser.

On a Chromebook

  • On your Chromebook, at the bottom right, click Time Settings .
  • On the left, select Privacy and security Privacy controls.
  • Turn on Camera access. On a macOS

On a macOS Mojave (version 10.14) or later, allow the browser to use your camera so Meet can use the camera.

  • On your macOS device, go to System Settings Privacy & Security.
  • Select Camera.
  • Check the box for the app that uses Google Meet.
    • For example: The app may be Google Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge. On a Windows computer
  • On your computer, click Start Settings.
  • Select Privacy & security Camera.
  • Turn on Camera access Allow apps access your camera. Tip: This setting lets users decide whether apps can use the camera.
Troubleshoot a black screen or crossed out camera icon

Check for camera hardware problems

  • On your device, open the built-in camera app, like Camera or Photo Booth.
  • If your camera’s self-preview shows your image but Meet doesn’t, make sure Meet can access your camera:
    • Enable camera access on macOS Mojave and later
    • Allow Google Chrome to use your camera
  • If your camera doesn’t show your image, check and adjust the camera cover or privacy switch. Open the camera cover or privacy switch

Important: Not all devices have a camera cover or privacy switch. If yours does:

  • The cover or switch might be at the top or side of your device.

  • Some models use an orange, red, or amber light when the privacy switch is on.

  • To find the camera cover, at the top of the camera lens, check for a slider.

    • For most devices, the camera cover is a physical slider above the lens.
      • For example, on Lenovo devices, the camera lens is blocked by the slider.

  • If there’s no slider above the lens, check for a physical switch on either side of your device.

    • Some devices use a privacy switch instead of a camera cover.
      • For example, the HP Chromebook has a camera privacy switch.

  • To unblock the camera lens, move the slider or switch to the off position.

  • Test the camera with the built-in Camera app or with Google Meet. Tip: If the camera’s self preview doesn’t show:

  • For Chromebook, try the steps to reset your Chromebook hardware.

  • For devices other than Chromebook, try more troubleshooting steps. Change the privacy mode in your camera settings

Important: Some devices have a software privacy switch.

  • On your device, go to Settings.
  • Find your camera settings.
  • Turn off the software-based privacy switch. Tip: The instructions might be different on your device.

Example of Chrome and Firefox browsers that shows camera lens blocked by software privacy switch.

Reset your Chromebook hardware

If there’s no camera cover or switch and the camera still doesn’t work:

  • Reset your Chromebook hardware.
  • Test the camera with the built-in Camera app or with Google Meet.

Troubleshoot connection issues with Google Meet

Troubleshoot connection issues with Google Meet

You can try the steps below to fix connection issues with Google Meet.

For Chrome OS specific issues, learn how to use diagnostics to troubleshoot your issue.

Verify service status

Check official status dashboards

  • On your computer, go to the Google Workspace Status Dashboard.
  • In the list of services, find Google Meet.
  • Check these icons for current status:
    • Green: Available
    • Orange: Service disruption
    • Red: Service outage
Check your own connection status

Check for in-app alerts

  • In your Google Meet call, click More options .
  • Select Troubleshooting & help.
  • For real-time information about your connection’s performance, review the Network stability graph and other diagnostics.
Reduce local system strain

Close unnecessary apps & browser tabs

  • Outside of the Google Meet window, close any software that isn’t essential for your meeting.

    • For example, close high-power or high-bandwidth apps like:
      • Streaming services
      • Video games
      • Cloud backup clients

  • Close any non-essential browser tabs. Pause large downloads or uploads

  • Check your system for:

    • Active file downloads
    • Software updates
    • Cloud file synchronization like Google Drive or Dropbox

  • Pause these activities for the duration of your meeting.

Exit & rejoin a meeting
  • In the bottom control bar, click Leave call .
  • To enter the same meeting again, on the screen that appears, click Rejoin.
Restart your computer or mobile device
  • During a Google Meet call, save your open work.
  • Restart your device.
  • After the reboot, rejoin the meeting.
Troubleshoot your local network

Learn how to fix connection and loading errors in Chrome.

Update your browser

To get the latest software fixes, learn how to update:

  • Google Chrome
  • Safari
  • Firefox
  • Microsoft Edge Restart Chrome browser

When you close Chrome after you update, it doesn’t fix the issue. The apps or extensions that use your microphone don’t reset. To reset these apps or extensions, restart Chrome.

  • In your browser, enter chrome://restart
    • When you restart Chrome, your tabs and windows reopen.
  • Turn on your microphone and camera.
  • Rejoin the video meeting.
Update your Operating System
  • On Windows: Click Settings Update & Security Windows Update Check for updates.
  • On macOS:
    • Click System Settings General Software Update.
    • Install any available updates.
Clear browser cache & data

Clear your browser cache

  • To clear your browsing data, click Settings.
    • In Chrome: Click Settings Privacy and security Clear browsing data.
  • Click Cached images and files.
  • Choose a time range.
    • For example, you can choose the last 24 hours.
  • Click Clear data.
  • Restart your browser.
Disable browser extensions

Temporarily disable extensions

  • In your browser, go to the extensions management page.
    • In Chrome: More options Extensions Manage Extensions.
  • To temporarily disable all extensions like ad blockers or privacy-related tools, use the toggle switch.
  • Restart your browser.
  • Try Google Meet again.
Temporarily disconnect from VPN or proxy
  • Open your VPN client software.
  • Disconnect from the VPN server.
  • In your system’s network settings, disable any proxy settings in your system’s network settings.
  • Try to rejoin the Google Meet call with a direct internet connection.
Turn off video to improve your connection

If your connection is poor, to turn off your video, click the Camera . This significantly reduces the amount of bandwidth your connection uses to stabilize your audio.

Troubleshoot issues when you join or create a meeting

Troubleshoot issues when you join or create a meeting

Here’s how to troubleshoot common joining and creating issues.

Update your browser

Update your browser to get the latest software fixes. Learn how to update Google Chrome.

Can’t create or join a Meet video meeting

​To create a new Meet video meeting or add a link in a Google Calendar event, you must be signed in to a Google account. Adding a link to a Google Calendar event is only available for users who have access to Google Calendar.

If you can join a Meet video meeting, but cannot create or add Meet video meetings, your administrator might need to turn on the meeting for your organization. Ask your administrator for more information.

Can’t join or create meetings from chat conversations

​If the meeting is turned off for your organization, you cannot join or create any Chat meetings. Ask your administrator for help.

Scheduled meetings don’t display
  • If you open Google Meet but don’t find any scheduled meetings, you might not have any scheduled meetings. Only meetings scheduled through Google Calendar will show up on meet.google.com or in your Meet app.
  • Make sure you’re signed in to your Google Workspace account for work or school, or your personal Google account. Make sure you can check you Gmail on the same device or computer.
Why is “Your meeting is full” displayed?

You can meet the maximum number of people for your Google Workspace edition.

  • Business Starter, Frontline, Education Fundamentals, G Suite Basic: 100 participants
  • Business Standard, Enterprise Essentials, Essentials, G Suite Business, Google Workspace for Non-profits: 150 participants
  • Business Plus, Enterprise Standard, Enterprise Plus, Education Plus: 500 participants Tip: The limits are for the number of device connections. Multiple people can join from a conference room or a shared device.

Important: Meetings created by a personal Google account have a limit of 100 participants.

For more information, go to Compare Google Workspace Editions.

Why is a network problem displayed?

​If a network transport timeout or firewall error is displayed, your group’s network might not be configured for meetings. For example, a required UDP and TCP port might be blocked.

Contact your Google Workspace or network administrators and ask them to optimize your network for Google Meet.

Meet is showing the wrong time

To change the time displayed in Meet, change your Google Calendar time zone setting.

A dial-in number is missing or for a different country

Important: Meet Global Dialing is available for meetings created by Google Workspace users.

  • All Google Workspace invites include a US phone number.
    • Some editions include additional numbers at no charge.
    • With Meet Global Dialing, Google Workspace accounts have access to numbers from additional countries. Phone charges may apply.
  • Calendar and Meet use your location to recommend a dial-in number.
  • If the location and time settings on your computer and Calendar are different, you may get different dial-in numbers on your device and in the Calendar invitation.
  • To check if your country is supported, go to supported countries for dialing into a meeting.
A dial-in number is not listed on my meeting

Important: This feature is currently available for meetings created by Google Workspace users.

If your administrator turns on the dial-in feature for Google Meet, all Google Workspace editions include a US phone number. G Suite Basic, G Suite Business, Google Workspace for Education Plus, Essentials, Business Starter, Frontline, Business Standard, Business Plus, Enterprise Essentials, Enterprise Standard, Enterprise Plus also support international numbers in Meet video meetings. Regular call charges apply.

Anyone can use the number to dial in, including external users and people using other Google Workspace editions.

To find if your country is supported, go to Supported countries for dialing into a meeting.

  • Google Meet training and help

Troubleshoot recording issues in meetings

Troubleshoot recording issues in meetings

Important:

  • The ability to record a meeting is only available on a computer.
  • Recording video meetings is only available for meetings organized by certain Google Workspace editions.
  • Participants can only record a meeting if the host has permission to record. Here’s how to troubleshoot issues when you record a meeting.

Learn how to record a video meeting.

Prompt shows up when I present or record in meetings on macOS Sequoia

If you’ve recently updated to macOS Sequoia:

  • Make sure to select “Allow” for Google Chrome permissions when prompted.

  • You’ll receive a cautionary prompt when you first attempt to record a meeting or share your screen. Here’s what you can do:

  • To allow Google Chrome to access your screen:

    • When you start a presentation or recording in a meeting, in the dialog, click Allow.

  • If you missed the initial dialog to allow permissions, you’ll need to update your system settings.

    • To add Google Chrome, give control access to screen and system audio recording on Mac. Learn why recording is disabled

Recording may be disabled if:

  • Your admin turned off recording.

  • Your Workspace edition doesn’t support recording.

  • Your Google Drive is disabled.

  • You aren’t allowed to record a specific video meeting.

  • You’re in a breakout room. Breakout rooms don’t support recordings.

  • Your admin doesn’t allow you to create new files in Drive.

  • The meeting organizer doesn’t have permission to record. Even if you have the necessary permissions as a participant, you can’t record a meeting if the host doesn’t have them. Check with your admin to make sure:

  • Meet supports recording for you and your organization.

  • Recording is on for video meetings. Can’t find the recording button

  • Confirm that your admin has turned on recording for Meet in the Google Admin console.

  • Verify that you’re using Meet on a computer. Recording is only available for the computer version.

  • You can’t record if you join only to present, such as from a laptop while already in a video conference room. Join the video meeting first, start presenting, and then record.

  • You can’t record if the meeting was created on a conference room device (such as Meet hardware), or was generated by another process, such as a Chrome plug in. Schedule the meeting in Calendar or be sure a person, and not a device, starts any ad-hoc meetings.

  • If you can no longer record a recurring meeting that used to allow recording, make sure the meeting organizer’s account is not disabled, which also disabled recordings for the meetings they organized. To fix this, delete the meeting from the Calendar event, save it, and add a new meeting code to recreate a meeting as the new owner. Can’t find the recording

  • Recordings must be generated and are not immediately available after the recording ends.

  • When ready, an email with the recording link is sent to the meeting organizer and the person who started the recording.

  • The recording link is also added to the Calendar event and saved to the meeting organizer’s Meet Recordings folder in My Drive. I used to be able to record a meeting but I’m unable to record it today

Check with your admin to make sure they have Turned on recording for video meetings. Learn more about Recording a video meeting.

My recording in Google Drive says “Still processing”

  • “Still processing” means that the recording is still being prepared to view.&
  • To play the recording immediately, select the file and click More Download . Double-click the downloaded file on your computer. What happens to my existing recordings after the COVID19 features expire for my organization?

Recordings will continue to be available in Drive.

Issues with presenting & recording meetings on macOS Sequoia

If you’ve recently updated to macOS Sequoia, you’ll receive a cautionary prompt when you first attempt to record a meeting.

Here’s what you can do:

  • To allow Google Chrome Canary to access your screen:
    • When you start a presentation or recording in a meeting, in the dialog, click Allow.
  • If you missed the initial dialog to allow permissions:
    • On your Mac device, click System Preferences Security & Privacy.
    • Select the Privacy tab.
    • In the list, click Screen Recording.
    • To allow an app, click Add .
    • Next to Google Chrome, check the checkbox. To test the new recording experience:
  • Update Chrome to version 129 or up.
  • On your Mac, open the Terminal.
  • Enter: open -b com.google.Chrome --args --enable-features=UseSCContentSharingPicker.
  • To execute the command, on your keyboard, press Enter.
  • Optional: Enable the flag in Chrome.
    • In the address bar, enter: chrome://flags.
    • Search for the flag “Use ScreenCaptureKit picker for stream selection.”
    • Next to the flag, click the Down arrow Enabled.
    • Restart Chrome. Tip: To avoid this issue, you can delay the update to macOS Sequoia until macOS 15.1 releases.

I shared the recording with someone, but they can’t download it

Make sure you allow others to download your files:

  • Open Google Drive.
  • Select the recording file and click Share or Share .
  • In the bottom right, click Advanced.
  • Uncheck the box next to “Disable options to download, print, and copy for commenters and viewers.”
  • Click Save changes Done.

Update your web browser

Restart Chrome to reset permissions

To reset permissions, you can’t just close Chrome. You must perform a full restart.

Troubleshoot common issues when you screen share

I can’t click the share my screen button

Ask the meeting host to find out if “Host management” is on. The meeting organizer could’ve turned off Host Management to limit screen sharing privileges.

I can’t find the right window to share my screen

Window selections are limited to open windows. Make sure the desired window isn’t minimized.

When I try to share my screen, I get an error

To fix your errors, you can:

  • Update your browser or operating system.
  • Check your browser permissions settings to screen share.
  • Check your computer permissions settings to screen share.
    • Learn more if you can’t share Mac computer screens.
  • Restart your computer. When I’ve viewing a presentation, I want to see it in full screen without participant tiles

Use Spotlight Mode.

  • In a meeting, click Menu .
  • Click Adjust View .
  • Choose Spotlight Mode.
  • At the bottom right corner of a presentation, click Enlarge .

Troubleshoot video & audio quality in a meeting

Troubleshoot video & audio quality in a meeting

Here’s how to fix common video and audio quality issues in a meeting.

Update your browser

Update your browser to get the latest software fixes. Learn how to update Google Chrome.

Use automatic troubleshooting & help

Troubleshooting & help gives automatic suggestions to fix quality issues with your network or devices during a meeting when an issue is detected that may affect the call quality.

If you have network or device issues that may affect the call quality, a red dot appears on the More options button.

  • When the dot appears, click More options Troubleshooting & help.
  • Tailored recommendations are shown based on your issue.
  • Try the suggestions.
  • The red dot shows for 5 minutes or until you click More options. Tip: The red dot only appears once a day, even if an issue persists.
Fix Echo warnings

If your audio has an echo, a red dot notification appears on the More options button:

  • Click More Troubleshooting & help.

  • Under “Audio & video devices,” you’ll find instructions to minimize the echo. Meet automatically tries to fix this echo. To help avoid an echo, you can:

  • Use headphones

  • Lower your speaker volume

  • Mute yourself when not speaking

Use the right peripherals

If audio or video is poor, try the following:

  • Use a headset with a microphone.
  • Make sure Meet is set to the correct camera, microphone and speakers. Headsets may use the built-in microphone.
    • Change your video and audio settings
  • Disconnect external monitors.
  • Make sure your bluetooth headset works with Meet. Some bluetooth headsets work well for normal audio calls but poorly with Meet.
  • Update your headset or camera to the latest firmware.
Turn off the video or join by phone or mobile app

If your computer is old or network performance is poor, join without video or switch to a different device.

  • Turn off the video
  • Join from the Meet mobile app
  • Dial in from a phone
  • Use a phone for audio in a video meeting
Improve your Wi-Fi or network performance

Bandwidth issues are a major cause of poor video quality. Even if your video and audio seem fine, other meeting participants may have trouble hearing you or seeing you. Try the following to improve your bandwidth issues:

  • Run an Internet speed test to ensure you have sufficient bandwidth and low latency. Observe the bandwidth and latency over time to make sure you have a stable connection, which is required for high quality video calling. See bandwidth requirements.
  • Use a wired Ethernet connection, if available, to see if the video quality improves.
  • Use the 5 GHz Wi-Fi connection instead of the more heavily used 2.4 GHz band.
  • Hardware firewalls and security devices that inspect or alter Meet traffic before routing it onward may cause poor video quality. Have your admin read Prepare your network. And finally, consider disabling Quality of Service (QoS) for Meet traffic. Some network equipment uses QoS to prioritize specific types of traffic, and Google Meet also performs network prioritization, which can cause poor video quality when combined with QoS. Temporarily disable QoS for Meet to see if video quality improves. See QoS best practices.
Deactivate VPN software

Your computer or smartphone normally connects directly to Meet. A VPN routes traffic through an additional network location and may delay video transmission to and from your Meet meeting.

  • Temporarily deactivate your VPN and reconnect to the Meet video meeting.
  • If video quality improves, complete the call without VPN.
  • Remember to deactivate the VPN when connecting to future Meet video meetings.
  • Ask your IT or VPN service provider to change your VPN configuration to allow Meet traffic to bypass the VPN. They may need to obtain information on the outbound ports, allowlisted URIs, and IP ranges for Meet. Refer them to the Prepare your network for Meet.
Close other browser tabs and apps

Too many tabs and open applications can cause poor video quality.

  • Close non-essential tabs.
  • Close other apps.
  • Reduce the size of the Meet window.
Talk to your system administrator

If you experiencing network issues, your system administrator may be able to help you resolve the issues.Try the following:

  • Ask your system administrator to analyze data from your video using the Meet Quality Tool.
  • In some cases, your corporate network may not be properly configured to access Google’s cloud for the highest quality results. Have your system administrator read Prepare your network.
Configure antivirus, firewall, or other security software
  • Software that inspects or alters Meet traffic before it reaches the video meeting may interfere with Meet and may cause poor video quality.
  • Review the options that allow the Chrome browser and Meet traffic to operate without interference. If you run into repeated issues, your admin may need to allowlist specific URLs for Meet to best operate. See Prepare your network.
Change your computer’s camera or video quality

You can decrease the quality of your video if you experience:

  • Video or audio delays
  • Poor network connection
  • Low battery
  • Limited data availability
  • Other quality issues

Try the new Google Meet Hardware touch controller UI

Try the new Google Meet Hardware touch controller UI

Important: The new touchscreen UI is available to all Google Workspace users with a Google Meet hardware license.

We’re launching a new touchscreen UI for Google Meet Hardware devices. The new UI is consistent with the Meet UI on desktops, laptops, and mobile devices.

Learn more about key benefits & changes

This update makes your meeting room experience smoother, more intuitive, and collaborative:

  • Familiar and intuitive: If you use Meet on desktops or laptops, you can find the touchscreen controls instantly recognizable. Jump right into your meeting without the need to search for buttons.

  • Focus on collaboration: You will spend less time managing technology and more time in productive discussions as the new controls are designed to make the prioritized buttons easier to find.

  • Consistent Meet experience: Enjoy a seamless and predictable interface whether you join from your personal device or a meeting room. For ease of use, the updated design organizes controls into 2 main areas:

  • Simple view: This is the default view when you’re in a meeting. It provides access to the most frequently used core controls, like:

    • Mute or unmute microphone
    • Turn camera on or off
    • Send reactions (Emojis)
    • Closed captioning
    • Raise hand
    • More actions
    • Increase or decrease volume slider
    • End call (Touch Controller UI Refresh: Annotated In-meeting Experience)

  • More actions menu: If you tap More actions , you can find secondary controls used for specific situations, which include:

    • Access chat
    • Camera controls
    • Presenting content
    • Managing participants (People list)
    • Changing layouts
    • Starting or stopping recording
    • Activities (Polls and Q&A)
    • Settings (Audio, video, and more) (Touch Controller UI Refresh: More actions menu)

(Touch Controller UI Refresh: Advanced View)

Frequently asked questions

Note: We update this section based on user feedback.

Where can I find features like Present, Chat & Layouts in the new UI?

To create a cleaner and more streamlined experience, we moved several controls into the More actions menu. When you tap “More actions ,” you can find options like “Present,” “Chat,” and “Layouts.”

How do I change cameras or access other camera controls?

You can find the advanced camera settings, like switching between cameras and accessing pan tilt zoom (PTZ) controls, located under More actions Camera Controls.

(Touch Controller UI Refresh: Camera Controls)

Is a light mode available for the new UI

The new UI is currently only available in dark mode.

Why is the volume bar smaller?

The volume bar was redesigned to be more compact. If your users can’t change the volume with the slider, they can tap the volume icons.

Can we roll back to the legacy experience?

No, there’s no rollback option. The new UI is available by default for all Meet Hardware users.

Important:

  • This feature requires an eligible Google Workspace edition or Google AI plan. Learn about Gemini features and plans.
  • This feature is available in the same languages as “Take notes for me.” Learn more about the available languages for “Take notes for me” in Google Meet. Tip: This feature supports one language at a time. Multiple languages spoken in the same meeting aren’t currently supported.

You can now capture notes for an existing meeting space from a scheduled meeting, or for impromptu and casual meetings that are in person. You don’t need to be in a meeting room to use this feature.

How to use the feature
  • On your computer, go to meet.google.com.
  • At the top, tap Take notes Start taking notes.
    • You can set your device nearby and it will use Gemini to document the meeting.
  • When notes are being taken, you can select Pause or Stop.
    • If you select “Pause,” it will pause both the transcription and note taking. If you want to resume taking notes again, tap Continue.
    • If you select “Stop,” a confirmation pop-up message shows, tap Stop taking notes. Tips:
  • If a user who is not in person wants to join the meeting, you can transition the meeting to a normal video call flow.
  • You’ll receive the notes doc in your email and in the Drive folder of whoever turned on the feature.
After you end the meeting

  • The meeting notes document is generated shortly after the meeting ends and is saved in the Drive folder of the person who turned on the feature. Tips:

  • Meeting notes documents follow the Meet retention policy that your organization has configured.

  • The meeting organizer must have the Workspace edition that includes “take in person notes for me.”

Troubleshooting issues

Sometimes, you may not be able to select this feature. It can be due to the following reasons:

  • The meeting organizer doesn’t have an eligible Workspace Edition.

  • If your Google Account is through your work or school, your admin may not have turned on “Take notes for me.”

  • Smart feature control is disabled. Learn how to enable Smart features. Sometimes, the meeting summary can be incomplete, inaccurate, or not generated. It can be due to the following reasons:

  • Meeting content may not have followed Google Meet Acceptable Use Policy.

  • There may have been connectivity issues during the meeting.

  • The meeting may not have been the recommended length of 15 minutes or more.

Use Adaptive Audio in Meet

Use Adaptive Audio in Meet

Important: This feature requires an eligible Google Workspace subscription. Learn about Gemini features and plans.

Please note that you can’t use adaptive audio with Meet hardware devices.

When you use adaptive audio, you can join meetings with multiple laptops in the same room without dedicated conferencing hardware.

The microphone and speakers in the room automatically detect and connect to the laptops of the different participants as they join the meeting room. Everyone can hear each other clearly without worrying about echo, disruptive audio feedback, or huddling around one laptop.

Automatic detection and setup

When Meet automatically detects the presence of multiple laptops in the same room, it switches to adaptive audio mode. In this mode, the microphones and speakers of the laptops are combined.

Use adaptive audio to share audio
  • On your computer, join a meeting with 2 or more computers in the same space.
  • If your audio is automatically merged with other devices, you’ll get a pop-up that says “To avoid feedback, your audio is merged with other devices nearby.”
    • If you are asked to manually confirm, click Merge mic & speakers.
  • When your audio is shared, you’ll see the Adaptive audio mic appear on the top left corner.
    • To be heard well, keep your microphone unmuted.
  • Users with merged audio are grouped together in their tiles and highlighted collectively when someone speaks.
Turn off adaptive audio

Important: Turning off adaptive audio may cause echo or a howling noise.

To turn off adaptive audio during a meeting:

  • At the bottom right, click Show everyone .

  • Next to your name click Menu Stop merging your audio . To permanently turn off adaptive audio:

  • In the meeting, at the bottom, click More Settings .

  • Under “Settings,” click Audio.

  • At the bottom, turn off Adaptive audio.

Use Adaptive Audio to share audio
  • On your computer, join a meeting with 2 or more computers in the same space.
  • Confirm you’re in the same location as other participants.
    • When a dialog in Meet pops up, click Share mic & speakers. Tip: The mute button changes to indicate that you share your audio.
About your microphone

You don’t need to mute yourself when you don’t speak. When you share audio, Meet automatically selects the microphone closest to the person in the room who speaks.

Since Meet uses all microphones in the room, you’re still heard if you mute your own microphone. If all microphones in the space are muted, you can’t be heard.

Troubleshooting
Fix issues with computer detection

If Meet doesn’t detect other computers in the room, make sure that:

  • The speakers of the computers aren’t fully muted.
  • Microphones with physical switches or in computers aren’t muted outside of Meet.
  • You turn off Voice Isolation macOS or Noise Suppression ChromeOS.
    • You can use Noise Cancellation in Meet with Adaptive Audio.
Fix echoes or bad audio quality
  • Audio problems usually disappear after a few seconds.
  • If problems persist, leave the meeting and join again.
    • If problems reoccur, use one computer.
Leave feedback in Meet

To help us improve this feature, submit feedback and describe the problem as accurately as possible. Make sure to include the text “Adaptive Audio” in your feedback so it is properly addressed.

Before a meeting
  • In a web browser, go to Google Meet.
  • Click Feedback .
  • Describe the issue or share your ideas.
  • To help us identify the issue, select Include screenshot.
  • Click Send. Tip: You can also click the meeting link or calendar event. Before you join, click More Report a problem.
In the meeting
  • Join a Google Meet meeting.
  • Click More .
  • Click Report a problem.
  • Describe the issue or share your ideas.
  • To help us identify the issue, select Include screenshot.
  • Click Send.
After the meeting

When the video meeting ends, click Submit feedback.

Use Google Meet with a screen reader

Use Google Meet with a screen reader

Topics

This article is divided into sections with headings. To jump to a specific section of the article, use the links below:

  • Quick start

    • Use recommended browser & screen readers

      • Use popup list of keyboard shortcuts

      • Present in a meeting

Quick start

Important: When you first join a meeting in Google Meet, in the browser dialog, allow camera and microphone access. Once you’re in the meeting, to easily toggle your:

  • Microphone:

    • On Windows or ChromeOS: Press Ctrl + d.
    • On macOS: Press Command + d.

  • Camera:

    • On Windows or ChromeOS: Press Ctrl + e.
    • On macOS: Press Command + e. To join a meeting:

  • Find your meeting:

    • On Google Meet.
    • On Google Calendar.
    • In an email link.

  • Open the meeting.

  • Tab to the Join now button and press Enter. To leave a meeting:

  • To return to the landing page or to quickly join another meeting, use the browser’s back function.

  • To just leave the meeting, close the browser tab.

    • On Windows or ChromeOS: Press Ctrl + w.
    • On macOS: Press Command + w.
Get started

If you’re logged in to your Google Account and a meeting is about to start, the landing page opens and the meeting subject is in focus. To join the meeting, press Enter.

Optional:

  • Join a meeting
  • Start a new meeting
Use recommended browser & screen readers

Use Google Meet with Chrome browser and these screen readers:

  • On Windows: NVDA or JAWS
  • On ChromeOS: ChromeVox
  • On macOS: VoiceOver
Set up your screen reader

Use your screen reader to navigate the Meet user interface as a web page. Since that’s the default for the supported screen readers, it doesn’t require additional set up.

Use screen reader navigation

To navigate the elements of the Google Meet user interface, use your screen reader commands. You can find most controls as buttons that you can activate. Once you learn what controls are available, you can use your screen reader search command to quickly navigate to a specific control.

Learn about the Meet interface

In the Meet user interface, you can find buttons for actions like:

  • Content presentation
  • Tiles which show some meeting participants
  • Action controls such as:
    • Camera toggle
    • Raise hand Some action buttons show and place keyboard focus on a sidebar or dialog with additional information.
Sidebars

A sidebar can be opened to present additional information in Meet. These include:

  • Chat: Activate the Chat with everyone toggle button. Learn how to chat with others.

    • On Windows or ChromeOS: Press Ctrl + Alt + c.
    • On macOS: Press Control + Command + c.

  • Participants: Activate the People toggle button. Learn how to find meeting participants.

    • On Windows or ChromeOS: Press Ctrl + Alt + p.
    • On macOS: Press Control + Command + p.

  • Meeting details: Activate the Meeting details toggle button. Learn how to find meeting details.

    • Tip: This also includes links to content shared with the meeting.

  • Visual effects: Activate the More options menu button, and then Apply visual effects.

  • Activities: Activate the Activities toggle button.

  • Host controls: Activate the Host controls toggle button. Tips:

  • To close a sidebar, activate the Close button or press Esc.

  • You can only open one sidebar at a time.

  • If you open another sidebar or try to reopen the same one, the current sidebar closes.

  • When a Meet dialog has focus, you can’t open a sidebar.

Dialogs

You can display a Meet dialog when a sidebar is open. You can’t display more than one dialog at the same time. The available dialogs include:

  • Shortcuts: To display the shortcuts dialog:
    • On Windows or ChromeOS: Press Ctrl + /.
    • On macOS: Press Control + Command + /.
  • Settings: To display a settings dialog, activate the More actions menu button, and then Settings.
  • Troubleshooting and help: To display a troubleshooting and help dialog, activate the More actions menu button, and then Troubleshooting & help. To close a dialog, activate the Close button or press Esc.
Keyboard shortcuts

These shortcuts also have equivalent UI buttons.

  • Turn the camera on or off:
    • For Windows or ChromeOS: Ctrl + e
    • For macOS: Command + e
  • Mute or unmute your microphone:
    • For Windows or ChromeOS: Ctrl + d
    • For macOS: Command + d
  • Show or hide meeting chat window:
    • For Windows or ChromeOS: Ctrl + Alt + c
    • For macOS: Control + Command + c
  • Show or hide participants:
    • For Windows or ChromeOS: Ctrl + Alt + p
    • For macOS: Control + Command + p
  • Raise or lower hand:
    • For Windows or ChromeOS: Ctrl + Alt + h
    • For macOS: Control + Command + h These shortcuts don’t have an equivalent in the UI and only produce screen reader output.
  • Announce who’s currently speaking:
    • For Windows or ChromeOS: Ctrl + Alt + s
    • For macOS: Control + Command + s
  • Announce current information about the room:
    • For Windows or ChromeOS: Ctrl + Alt + i
    • For macOS: Control + Command + i
  • Announce recently received reactions:
    • For Windows or ChromeOS: Ctrl + Alt + x
    • For macOS: Control + Command + x To review all shortcuts available in Meet, in Use Google Workspace keyboard shortcuts page, check the list of Meet keyboard shortcuts.
Use popup list of keyboard shortcuts
  • To open a dialog with more than one table of keyboard shortcuts:
    • On Windows or ChromeOS: Press Ctrl + /.
    • On macOS: Press Control + Command + /.
  • Review or filter the keyboard shortcuts.
    • To review: Use screen reader table navigation commands.
    • To filter: In the focused search field, enter the text. Tip: Based on your screen reader, to perform some shortcuts, you need to toggle between web navigation and focus navigation.
Windows keyboard shortcut considerations

If you use a keyboard layout other than US English, shortcuts with Ctrl + Alt won’t work correctly and act like you pressed AltGr. To use the shortcuts, consult the Windows documentation on how to install and temporarily switch to the US English keyboard layout.

Links

To prevent unintentional exits from the meeting, links in Google Meet’s pre-call and in-call experiences open in a new tab or window. Meet doesn’t include this as a supplemental accessible label.

Complete common tasks
Join a meeting

To join a meeting in Google Meet:

  • Open a meeting through a link or the landing page.

  • In the Meet preview page, to turn your microphone and camera on or off:

    • Tab to the Turn on microphone or Turn off microphone button and press Enter.
    • Tab to the Turn on camera or Turn off camera button and press Enter.

  • Optional: To apply visual effects like an alternative or blur background:

    • Tab to the Apply visual effects button and press Enter.
    • Select the visual effects.

  • To join the meeting, tab to the Join now button and press Enter. You can use “Other ways to join” if you also want to:

  • Present when you join.

  • Use companion mode.

  • Use a phone to listen to the meeting.

  • Connect to a conference room.

Leave a meeting

To leave a meeting, you can either:

  • Close the browser tab:
    • On Windows or ChromeOS: Press Ctrl + w.
    • On macOS: Press Command + w.
  • Leave the meeting and return to the landing page:
    • On Windows or ChromeOS: Press Alt + Left arrow.
    • On macOS: Press Command + Left bracket.
  • Leave the meeting: Activate the Leave call button. Tip: The meeting ends when the last person leaves.
Start a new meeting

To start a new meeting, open Google Meet. A landing page opens in one of 3 variations, if you’re:

  • Logged in and a meeting is about to start:
    • If you’re logged in to your web browser with a Google Account and a meeting from your calendar is about to start:
      • The landing page opens with focus on the meeting that’s about to start.
      • To join the meeting, press Enter.
    • There are also options to start a new meeting or join a meeting with a code.
  • Logged in without a scheduled meeting:
    • If you’re logged in to your web browser with a Google Account, but no meeting is about to start, the landing page opens with focus on the first past meeting of that day.
    • To start a new meeting, press Enter. It opens a menu with these options:
      • Create a meeting for later: Opens a dialog with a URL, a phone number, and a PIN. To copy this information to the clipboard, activate the Copy joining info button.
      • Start an instant meeting: Immediately starts a meeting. To add participants, in the “Your meeting’s ready” dialog, activate the Add others or Copy link button.
        • Tip: To familiarize yourself with the available controls during a meeting, use this with no other participants.
      • Schedule in Google Calendar: Opens a new event in Google Calendar.
      • Video call options: Based on your account, this presents encryption options.
  • Not logged in:
    • If you’re not logged in to your web browser with a Google Account, the landing page opens with no initial focus.
    • If you have a code to join a meeting:
      • Activate the Enter code button.
      • To join the meeting, enter the code.
    • Enter the URL sent by the host into the address bar of your web browser.
Find meeting participants
  • To open the participants sidebar, activate the People toggle button or:
    • On Windows and ChromeOS: Press Ctrl + Alt + p.
    • On macOS: Press Control + Command + p.
  • To identify the name and role of each participant, use screen reader navigation commands.
  • To find a participant, tab to the Search for people entry field, type part of their name or address, and then press Enter.
  • When participants raise their hand, the sidebar shows a “Raised hands” section.
    • In the “Raised hands” section, you can find the total number of raised hands and the participants in the order they raised their hand.
  • To close the sidebar and return focus to the Meet UI, press the shortcut again.
Chat with others
  • To open the meeting chat sidebar, activate the Chat with everyone toggle button or:
    • On Windows and Chrome OS: Press Ctrl + Alt + c.
    • On macOS: Press Control + Command + c.
  • In the chat sidebar, the keyboard focus moves to the entry field to “Send a message.”
  • To read previous messages and sender, use your screen reader “previous item” navigation.
  • To close the sidebar and return focus to the Meet UI, press the shortcut again. Tip: To enable new chat notifications, some screen readers and platforms require the chat sidebar to be open.
Find meeting details

To open the “Meeting details” sidebar, activate the Meeting details button.

In the “Meeting details” sidebar, you can find:

  • Joining information:

    • Meeting link
    • Dial-in number
    • PIN

  • Tip: To copy the “Joining info,” activate the Copy joining info link.

  • File attachments such as Slides presentation.

  • Agenda. Tips:

  • When you invite others to join the meeting, you can paste the joining information that you copy.

  • To easily follow the agenda or presentation, in a new tab, open the file attachment.

Change Meet settings

To open the Settings dialog:

  • In a meeting, tab to the More options button and press Enter.
  • To navigate to “Settings,” press Down arrow.
    • Press Enter.
  • In the “Settings” dialog, to navigate between the tabs, press Tab.
    • The “Audio” tab is selected by default.
    • You can find these 5 tabs in the settings:
      • Audio
      • Video
      • General
      • Captions
      • Reactions
  • To select the tab, press Spacebar.
    • The settings for the selected tab are after the “Reactions” tab in the tab order. Tips:
  • When you make changes in the settings, it takes effect immediately. There’s no need for “OK” or “Cancel” actions.
  • To close the Settings and return to the meeting, press Esc or activate the Close button.
Present in a video meeting

You can present a tab, a specific window, or the entire screen in a meeting. While you present, you can share information such as documents, presentations, and spreadsheets.

Present in a meeting
  • To open the “Choose what to share” dialog, activate the Present now button.
  • You can choose to:
    • Share a tab (selected by default):
      • Tab to the list of browser tabs.
      • To navigate to the tab you want to present, press Down arrow.
        • If you present a Chrome tab, it shares the tab audio by default.
    • Share a window (press right arrow once):
      • Tab to the list of windows.
      • To navigate to the window you want to present, press Down arrow.
        • It doesn’t share the audio.
    • Share your entire screen (press right arrow twice):
      • If you have more than one screen, tab to the list of screens.
      • To navigate to the screen you want to present, press Down arrow.
        • It doesn’t share the audio.
  • Press Enter or activate the Share button. Tip: With “Present now,” you can’t share system and screen reader audio.
Present with screen reader output

Important: This routes your screen reader audio output to the meeting and silences your computer. To also hear your screen reader audio, you can join with a second system or on your phone.

  • Open a meeting in Google Meet.

  • Tab to the Other ways to join button and press Enter.

  • Shift + Tab to the Present button and press Enter.

  • If the “Choose what to share” dialog opens:

    • Tab to the Chrome Tab button.
    • To navigate to the “Entire Screen,” press Left arrow.

  • Tab to and switch on: “Also share system audio. This device will be muted to prevent feedback.” Tips:

  • If you want to present your screen reader audio and still hear it on your system, use an external microphone.

  • Position the microphone to clearly pick up both your voice and the system’s audio output.

Stop presentation
  • On your browser, open the meeting tab.
  • Tab to the You are presenting button and press Enter.
  • To navigate to the “Stop presenting,” press Left arrow.
    • Press Enter. Tip: When you exit or close the meeting tab, your presentation stops.

To share files in a meeting, present from Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides, or other scenarios, learn how to present during a video meeting.

Learn about Google Meet Help

You can find links for more topics and scenarios in Google Meet Help. Some features are only available for certain Meet versions or account types.

Related resource
