Use Google Meet with Apple CarPlay

Use Google Meet with Apple CarPlay

To safely join meetings and make calls while you drive, you can use Google Meet on Apple CarPlay. It provides a simplified, audio-focused experience designed to reduce distractions.

Learn what you need to use Apple CarPlay
  • A vehicle that supports Apple CarPlay.
  • A connection between your iPhone to your vehicle via Bluetooth or a USB cable.
  • An updated Meet app on your Apple device. Tip: If you’re not signed into Meet, you receive a prompt to sign in.
Join a meeting or call

Important: Meetings joined from Apple CarPlay skip the pre-call screen.

  • Connect your iPhone to your vehicle through Bluetooth or a USB cable.
  • On your Apple CarPlay display, tap the Meet app .
Join a scheduled meeting
  • On your Apple CarPlay display, tap the Scheduled tab.
    • This tab shows your upcoming meetings.
  • From the list, select a meeting to join.
    • Your video is off automatically.
    • Your microphone might be automatically muted if you join a large meeting.
Call a recent contact or a group

  • On your Apple CarPlay display, tap the History tab.

  • Select the person or group you want to call. Tips:

  • If you need to use video or other features, such as Chat or Polls, safely park your car. Then, use your mobile phone to do so on the Meet app.

  • You join the meeting on both your iPhone and car display.

  • If the host turns on a waiting room, you get a status message on your screen until they admit you.

  • Your audio switches automatically:

    • When you connect your phone to CarPlay: Your audio transfers from your phone or earbuds to the car’s speakers.
    • When you disconnect your phone from CarPlay: Your audio returns to your phone, earbuds, or the previously used output device.
Use in-meeting controls

While in a meeting, use the controls on your car’s display:

  • Mute or unmute: To change your audio, tap Mic .
  • Leave a meeting: To exit and return to the Meet home screen, tap End .
Manage permissions & setup

If you’re not signed into Meet or haven’t granted permissions, you’ll be prompted to do so:

  • When safe, check your iPhone for permission prompts or the sign in screen.
  • To turn on calling features, grant mic access.
  • To continue the use of car display, make sure you acknowledge any privacy prompts on your phone.
Learn more about the in-call experience
  • Safe driving mode: When you connect to CarPlay, your iPhone automatically enters On-the-Go mode. This shows a simplified mobile UI.
  • Display: Only the call info and controls are visible, not presentations or other participants.
  • Audio notifications: If a meeting is being recorded, transcribed, or using Gemini, you hear spoken notifications.
  • Limited interactions: To meet safety standards while you drive, you can’t use features like Hand Raise, Q&A, or Polls.
  • Breakout rooms: If a breakout room is created, you automatically move into it. When the breakout room session ends, you return to the main room. Note: Meeting hosts can’t admit or reject participants from the car controls.

Tip: When you join Apple CarPlay from your car, your video is off by default. If you need to use video or other features, such as Chat or Polls, safely park your car. Then, use your mobile phone to connect to the Meet app.

Use Meet on Android Auto

Use Meet on Android Auto

To safely join meetings and make calls from your personal account while you drive, you can use Google Meet on Android Auto. It provides a simplified, audio-focused experience designed to reduce distractions.

Important: Work profile accounts aren’t supported in Meet on Android Auto. Active calls will still appear on your display but upcoming meetings and call history will not show.

Learn what you need to use Android Auto
  • A vehicle that supports Android Auto.
  • A connection between your Android phone to your vehicle through Bluetooth or a USB cable.
  • An updated Meet app on your Android device. Tip: If you’re not signed into Meet, you receive a prompt to sign in.
Join a meeting or call

Important: Calls and meetings joined from Android Auto skip the pre-call screen.

  • Connect your phone to your vehicle through Bluetooth or a USB cable.
  • Tap Android Auto.
  • On your Android Auto display, tap the Meet app .
Join a scheduled meeting
  • On your Android Auto display, tap the Scheduled tab.
    • This tab shows your upcoming meetings.
  • From the list, select a meeting.
  • Tap Join.
    • Your video is off automatically.
    • Your microphone might be automatically muted if you join a large meeting.
Call a recent contact or a group

  • On your Android Auto display, tap the History tab.

  • Select the person or group you want to call. Tips:

  • You join the meeting on both your Android phone and car display.

  • If the host turns on a waiting room, you get a status message on your screen until they admit you.

  • Your audio switches automatically.

    • When you connect your phone to Android Auto: Your audio transfers from your phone or earbuds to the car’s speakers.
    • When you disconnect your phone from Android Auto: Your audio returns to your phone, earbuds, or the previously used output device.

  • If you need to use video or other features, such as Chat or Polls, safely park your car. Then, use your mobile phone to do so on the Meet app.

Use in-meeting controls

While in a meeting or call, use the controls on your car’s display:

  • Mute or unmute: To change your audio, tap Mic .
  • Leave a meeting: To exit and return to the Meet home screen, tap Hang up .
Answer calls

Your car’s screen shows the caller’s info for incoming calls.

  • To answer the call, tap Answer.
  • To ignore the call, tap Decline.
Manage permissions & setup

If you use the app for the first time or haven’t granted permissions, you may receive an “Attention” prompt:

  • When safe, check your Android phone for permission prompts.
  • To turn on calling features, grant mic access.
  • To continue the use of car display, make sure you acknowledge any privacy prompts on your phone.
Learn more about the in-call experience
  • Safe driving mode: When you start a meeting or call from Android Auto, your phone automatically enters On-the-Go mode. This shows a simplified mobile UI.
  • Display: Only the call info and controls are visible, not presentations or other participants.
  • Audio notifications: If a meeting is being recorded, transcribed, or using Gemini, you hear spoken notifications.
  • Limited interactions: To meet safety standards while you drive, you can’t use features like Hand Raise, Q&A, or Polls.
  • Breakout rooms: If a breakout room is created, you automatically move into it. When the breakout room session ends, you return to the main room. Note: Meeting hosts can’t admit or reject participants from the car controls.

Use the Google Meet homepage

Use the Google Meet homepage

You can use the new Google Meet homepage at meet.google.com to prepare for, organize, and manage your video meetings. This centralized hub helps you quickly start or join meetings, find scheduled meetings, and access important meeting resources.

Start or join a meeting

You can quickly start or join a meeting at the top of the homepage in a few different ways.

  • Create a new meeting: Click New to create a new meeting, then select one of the following options:
    • Create a meeting for later: Creates a meeting link you can share.
    • Start an instant meeting: Immediately creates and opens a new meeting.
    • Schedule in Google Calendar: Opens Google Calendar to create a new event with Meet details.
  • Join a meeting: In the text box at the top, enter a meeting code, meeting URL, or a nickname, then click Join.
Find your daily meetings

The homepage shows a list of your daily meetings, organized into distinct sections to help you keep track of your schedule.

  • Find scheduled meetings: The “Scheduled” section shows current and upcoming meetings for the selected day. Current meetings already in progress appear as “Happening Now” and are highlighted in blue for easy identification.
  • Find past meetings: The “Past” section displays your meetings that have already happened. It collapses by default to keep your agenda tidy. Select Show more to find older past meetings, or Show less to collapse it again.
Open meeting attachments & resources

Directly access meeting resources from the homepage to review materials before or after a call. Meetings include quick links to important documents and post-meeting summaries.

  • Find file attachments: These files include Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, and PDFs added by the meeting organizer to the calendar invitation.
  • Find post-meeting resources: These are quick links to items such as Recordings, Transcripts, and “Notes by Gemini” summaries. These resources are automatically created if you use the “Take Notes for Me” feature during the meeting.
Check meetings on a different date

Easily navigate your schedule and view meetings on other dates using the available options.

  • Use the week selector: Select any day within the week near the top of the page to quickly view meetings for that specific day. Use the left and right arrows to go to previous or future weeks.
  • Choose a date on a calendar: Select the calendar next to the current date to open a calendar menu and select any specific date from the calendar.
  • Go to today’s date: Select the Today button to go back to meetings for today’s date.
My homepage looks different

If you’re using Google Meet in Germany with a personal account, you might not see your list of daily meetings on the homepage. You can use Google Calendar to see your upcoming meetings.

Your audio & video data stays private with video messages sent in Google Meet

Your audio & video data stays private with video messages sent in Google Meet

To keep your data private, video or voice messages on the Meet app are protected with end-to-end encryption. Only the sender and receiver can know what’s said or shown, and Google can’t see or hear your video or voice messages. However, when you turn on captions, your audio data is sent to Google’s Cloud transcription service. No video data is sent and your audio content isn’t linked with any personal identifiers. Google doesn’t save any data as part of this feature.

Learn how to leave and check messages.

How messages work

You can send video or voice messages with the new Meet app. You can also turn on captions for video or voice messages you send and receive.

After you play a message, you can revisit it at any time unless you changed your Meet calling settings to automatically delete video or voice messages 24 hours after they play. When your messages automatically delete, they are removed from all your devices.

How we protect your data

Google Meet video and voice messages are sent with end-to-end encryption. This means that the message’s audio and video data are encrypted from your device to your contact’s device. The encrypted audio and video can be decoded only with a shared secret key. You can learn more in Duo’s end-to-end encryption technical paper.

However, to provide captions, audio data from your video or voice message is sent to Google’s Cloud speech service. Personal identifiers are removed before the audio data is sent so this audio is not linked to you.

Your video or voice messages are encrypted when they’re sent to Google’s Cloud speech service and while they’re on Google’s storage system for captioning. Google doesn’t read your messages or keep your audio data.

You’re in control
Turn on captions
  • On your Android phone or tablet, open Google Meet .
  • At the top left corner, tap Menu Settings Calling settings Message Settings.
  • Turn on Captions for messages.
Delete messages after 24 hours
  • On your Android phone or tablet, open Google Meet .
  • At the top left corner, tap Menu Settings Calling settings Message Settings.
  • Turn off Save Messages.

  • Take screenshots of 1:1 and group video calls Android iPhone & iPad

Your facial data stays private with video calling Effects & Portrait Mode

Your facial data stays private with video calling Effects & Portrait Mode

You can add effects to personalize your 1:1 and group video call or apply a portrait filter to make you look sharper against your background with Effects and Portrait Mode. To keep your data private, Google Meet processes your video data in real time when it is sent to other users in the video call but does not store any video data on your device or on Google servers.

How Effects & Portrait Mode work

We use images of your face taken by your camera to give you extra effects during 1:1 and group video calls. While this occurs during a 1:1 or group video call, Meet doesn’t store any personal or facial data on your device or on Google servers. Meet processes the video frames in real-time and each frame is deleted once it is processed and sent to other users in the video call.

How we protect your data

Facial data is only used to apply effects to 1:1 and group video calls on your device. Meet applies these effects to the images with machine learning technology that works on your device before they’re sent, so all images, 1:1 and group video calls, and effects are protected with end-to-end encryption. No data is stored on your device or sent to Google servers. Learn more about how your video calls & meetings stay encrypted.
